_about: Catalogue of unsolved historical ciphers not on the Tomokiyo, Schmeh or Dunin lists, plus (since 14 Oct 2026) open items pulled from Cryptoole (research/cryptoole/), some of them on Tomokiyo's list; those carry source "Cryptoole" and their Cryptoole ID in "cryptoole". Scores are 1-5 and unvalidated: importance = historical weight of what the text could add; solvability = odds of a full reading with the material available online; difficulty = technical work needed (1 trivial key alignment, 5 statistics-only on an unknown system). Priority is computed on the page from adjustable weights. Class A = siblings with decipherment in the same volume, B = partial key or known family in print, C = no key, no sibling. seen: image = leaf viewed on the Gallica image; catalogue = selected from the catalogue description only. outcome: 'attempted, open' once an entry has been taken to the leaf here without a reading. Entries read, partly read, resolved or found already in print are removed from this file (19 Sept 2026) and recorded in SOLVED_CATALOGUE.md; ids are not reused. contributed_by: the contributors.json id of an outside contributor who brought the entry in (shown on the page as 'via ...'). Vetting gate (28 Oct 2026): an entry enters this file only with a complete "vetting" block (scan seen, prior art checked in DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry, the edition and the literature, held keys tried, duplicates searched); unvetted leads wait in research/leads.json and are promoted with docs/_check_catalogue.py --promote. Entries below 861 predate the gate. See README Conventions, "Catalogue vetting bar".

entries.title: Espagnol 318 nos. 92, 93, 94: Ferdinand's secretariat ciphers (Great Captain 1500, Suárez de Figueroa 1504, viceroy of Sicily 1503)
entries.correspondents: Lorenzo Suárez de Figueroa (Venice) → the Catholic Monarchs
entries.shelfmark: BnF Espagnol 318 no. 93
entries.folio_note: ff. 118-118v = canvases 446-447
entries.status: Widened again 23 Oct 2026 (Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): no. 92 and no. 94 are decoded, not read, so they are back here). Narrowed 21 Oct 2026 to no. 93. The entry first covered five ciphered letters in at least four ciphers: no. 5 (Escrivà's cipher, printed by Parisi 2020; targets/federico1497/), no. 92 (Cifra general, read in part; targets/esp318/) and no. 95 (recto deciphered in full by George Lasry with his CTTS key, PR #75, 22 Oct 2026; verso by Michael Brackx; targets/esp318no95/) have their own entries, and no. 94 (the viceroy of Sicily, Messina 1503) was split off on 21 Oct 2026 after Michael Brackx recovered its key ciphertext-only and read part of its code (issue #62; targets/esp318no94/). No. 93 is unread and its key unknown: code initials exclude Escrivà no. 1 and the Cifra general; a homophonic anneal of 1,016 signs failed (the CVC groups are atomic); no. 94's key does not fit and the two code inventories barely overlap. See targets/esp318no93/.
entries.why: The earliest Spanish diplomatic ciphers online; the Naples war (Cerignola, Garigliano) and Venice 1504.
entries.score_note: Rescored by hand 14 Oct 2026 after the split: no key in hand for either letter; the Gran cifra survives only as Bergenroth's partial list (BNE MSS 20.211/52, not online) and the 'Cifra del visorrey' (BRAH 9/15 ff. 1-6) is unpublished.
entries.verify: Transcribe no. 94 ff. 120r-121v (clear-text islands give context) and test Bergenroth's Gran-cifra list before a cold break.
entries.known: Nothing for nos. 93 and 94: keys not identified; a homophonic anneal of 1,016 signs of no. 93 failed (esp318no93.html). Former siblings: no. 5 printed by Parisi 2020 (federico1497), no. 92 about 75% deciphered with the Cifra general (esp318), no. 95 recto deciphered in full by George Lasry with his own key (esp318no95, PR #75).
entries.open: No. 93 (f. 118r-v) whole letter: CVC nomenclator, the suspected Gran cifra key survives only as Bergenroth's partial list (BNE MSS 20.211/52, not online). No. 92 (targets/esp318/): decoded with the Cifra general (Galende Díaz 1994), not yet built into sentences. No. 94 (targets/esp318no94/): Michael Brackx's key recovered ciphertext-only, about 90 code groups open; his decryption has holes in most sentences.
entries.status_append: 2 Nov 2026 vetting: f. 118r viewed, about 35 lines of sign cipher, no gloss; keys of nos. 5, 92, 94, 95 do not read it.

entries.title: A Venetian secretary to the Venetian ambassador in England, 1625, in a three-figure syllabic code (SP 106/10 ff. 193-195)

entries.status: Attempted, open (21 Sept 2026; restored 14 Oct 2026 for sp106r722). entries.title: Johann Joachim von Rusdorff to Axel Oxenstierna, The Hague, 1628, three letters in cipher (R4333-R4335)
entries.correspondents: unknown → Camerarius?, Amsterdam; Rusdorff → Oxenstierna; Swedish agent → Oxenstierna
entries.shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Oxenstierna af Södermöre, Ser. B, E 701 (DECODE R4333-R4335)
entries.status: DECODE R4284–R4341, 8 records in four different ciphers, each its own entry since the one-key split of 14 Oct 2026. Viewed 21 Sept 2026. The two Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330–R4331, riksarkivet1628.html) are read and removed from this entry; R4282 was deciphered by George Lasry (decode4282.html). R4306: contributed partial Dutch decipherment by George Lasry, transcribed with CTTS then solved with Opus 5.5 (17 Oct 2026; sweden4306.html, which also records this project's failed attempt of 21 Sept 2026); pencilled 1632? and Amsterdam attribution remain qualified, four code identities open. R4336–R4337 turned out to be Rusdorff's London letters of February 1625 in a homophonic cipher with an alphabetical nomenclator; key recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry (21 Oct 2026, PR #72; rusdorff1625.html) and removed from this entry. Open: R4284 (Latin 1628, Camerarius docket; riksarkivet4284.html) — attacked with Latin annealing and against two box keys, not broken; R4333–R4335 (Rusdorff → Oxenstierna 1628, another cipher; rusdorff1628.html) and R4338–R4341 (E 708, Swedish, June 1633, not 1646; glossed in part at the time; oxenstierna1633.html) surveyed only. Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
entries.why: One remaining key-box ciphertext that resisted a first attack, and Oxenstierna correspondence of 1628 and 1633 with a key collection that may hold their keys.
entries.score_note: Scored by rule from DECODE metadata (class from key signals, solvability from key, length and language, importance from the correspondents); not yet reviewed by hand.
entries.verify: Fetch the images and the key record(s); test the key on the first lines.
entries.known: Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330-R4331) deciphered in full here, key recovered from the interlinear glosses (riksarkivet1628). R4282 key recovered ciphertext-only by George Lasry (decode4282, PR #33). R4306 deciphered in part by George Lasry with CTTS and Opus 5.5, 17 Oct 2026 (sweden4306, PR #42); four code values open. R4336-R4337 (Rusdorff, London, Feb 1625) key recovered ciphertext-only by George Lasry with CTTS and Claude Opus 5.5, 21 Oct 2026 (rusdorff1625, PR #72); codes 628 and 701 open.
entries.open: All cipher passages; surveyed only (targets/rusdorff1628). The rusdorff1625 key does not fit R4333.

entries.title: Gerard Carel baron van Spaen tot Voorstonden, envoy of the King of Holland (Düsseldorf), to Maarten van der Goes, minister of foreign affairs, 14 and 15 Jan 1808
entries.correspondents: G. C. van Spaen tot Voorstonden, envoy of the King of Holland → Maarten van der Goes (1751-1826), minister of foreign affairs
entries.shelfmark: NA The Hague, 02.01.08., Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken, 1796-1810, inv. nr. 281
entries.status: DECODE R1941, viewed 21 Sept 2026 (targets/spaen1808/). Two items: the letter of 14 Jan 1808 (228 groups) and an annex of 15 Jan (75 groups; DECODE images P1 and P2 are two photos of the same page). Plain numerical code, groups 15-1339, no marks, dashes as separators; clear openings and closings in Dutch. No decipherment on the images, and DECODE holds no key for it (the 1798 and 1803 Croiset books R1891/R1035 do not fit). DECODE's 'annex solved' has no reading attached to the record. Not in Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken V (searched). 303 groups, 222 distinct, from a code of 1,300+ entries: not breakable without the key. NA inventory: inv. 281 = letters of J.F.G. van Spaen and G. van Riemsdijk, commissioners for the takeover of the ceded districts (Lijmers, Huissen, Malburgen, Zevenaar), 1806-09; Düsseldorf = Grand Duchy of Berg, not Westphalia. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): dated Düsseldorf, 12 January 1808 (No. 4); 14 January is the date of receipt ('Exh'). Two-part code, not breakable without a crib.

entries.title: Siena, "Lettere in cifra" of the Concistoro: the pieces still unsolved (nos. 4, 7, 14, 15, 19, 21; no. 1 of 1421 unphotographed)
entries.correspondents: Sienese envoys and others → the Concistoro of Siena
entries.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308, fasc. 2 "Lettere in cifra": nos. 7, 19, 21 (R4796, R4807, R4809); no. 1 (1421), 2, 26-28 (not on DECODE)
entries.status: Narrowed 18 Oct 2026 to the pieces still unsolved, after George Lasry's report of 17 Oct 2026 (one entry per key; index research/siena2308/). Open: no. 7 (R4796, orator at Milan to the Balia, 1450s; 363 signs, interlinear gloss gives nine values; filed key R4750 and five others fail it; targets/siena7/), no. 19 (R4807, Sienese envoys, 9 March, 1440s; 118 signs; targets/siena19/), no. 21 (R4809, 'Karissimo come padre', 15th c.; 107 signs; targets/siena21/): attempted, too short without a key. No. 1 (1421) and nos. 2, 26-28 are not among the DECODE photographs (needs ASSi). The other pieces are deciphered on their own entries: nos. 20/23, 12, 6/24, 25, 11, 18, 17, 5?, 9, 13/16, 10 and 8 (no. 8 from the contemporary decipherment on its sheet, aligned here 18 Oct 2026). 23 Oct 2026, Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): no. 4 (R4793, Borghesi 1456; targets/borghesi1456/), no. 14 (R4802; targets/siena14/) and no. 15 (R4803; targets/siena15/) are decoded, not read, and are back among the open pieces.
entries.why: Nos. 7, 19 and 21 are the last undeciphered 15th-century pieces of the Sienese file. No. 1 (1421) would not be its oldest letter: George Lasry's decipherments include letters of March and April 1413 (nos. 12, 20, 23; the years reconstructed, not written).
entries.verify: Order nos. 1, 2, 26-28 from ASSi; for nos. 7, 19, 21 look for a sibling letter in the same key or a fresh transcription in CTTS (no. 7: rerun with the gloss values fixed).
entries.known: Every other photographed piece is deciphered on its own entry (index: siena1421.html). George Lasry recovered the keys of no. 12, 10 March 1413 (the year reconstructed from the sixth indiction and the context), nos. 20 and 23, 30 March and about April 1413 (years inferred), nos. 6/24, 9, 11, 13/16, 17, R4794 and no. 15 in part; this project recovered nos. 4, 18, 25 and no. 14 in part; nos. 8 and 10 were deciphered at the time. No. 7: the interlinear gloss gives nine values.
entries.open: Nos. 7 (R4796, 363 signs), 19 (R4807, 118) and 21 (R4809, 107): no key; none of the filed keys fits, and neither George Lasry nor this project has deciphered them. No. 1 (Meister's 1421 letter), 2 and 26-28 are not photographed; they need the Archivio di Stato di Siena. No. 4 (R4793, 144 signs): key rebuilt from an alphabet fragment and the glosses, 114 signs given a value, no sentences. No. 14 (R4802): key recovered from the ciphertext alone, L01-L26 decoded, not read. No. 15 (R4803): partly deciphered by George Lasry by crib guessing (no key filed), decoded, not read.

entries.status: Cryptoole IT1498-1 (open). entries.status: Cryptoole XX1678-1 (open). Attempted 27 Oct 2026, not solved (targets/ormond1678/). 20 figures, all distinct: 445 and 342 before two runs ('726 91 33 425 93 58 384 54 700 720' and '732 573 526 32 643 214 55 440'). The sixth figure of run 1 is printed 58 on the p. 93 scan; '57' came from Tomokiyo's quotation. The calendar gives no gloss. The 1678 Ormond-Arran code of Arran's 9 Feb letter (pp. 105-106) is a two-letter code, so it cannot be this one. The Ormond-Longford 1680 key puts the low figures on bare consonants (l, k, m, h), as in Tomokiyo's rejected trial. Too short and repeat-free for a ciphertext-only attack.

entries.open: All 20 numbers: not deciphered; the 1678 Ormond-Arran code is not rebuilt and the manuscript (Ormonde papers, NLI) is unlocated; very short.

entries.title: Fragments in Girolamo Sirtori's cipher broken by Luis Valle de la Cerda (BNE Mss/994)
entries.correspondents: unknown writer using Girolamo Sirtori's cipher; handed to Luis Valle de la Cerda by a secretary of the Council of State
entries.shelfmark: Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional, Mss/994, ff. 83-90 (ciphertext ff. 85-87); BDH bdh0000174344
entries.status: Cryptoole ITXXXX-1 (partly solved). Valle broke it and said he had devised the same scheme fifteen years earlier; his solution is not extant. Transcription by Sara Gómez Hernández; partial Latin reading by Eloy Caballero (2012) on Cipher Mysteries. Review 20 Oct 2026: Caballero explicitly presents a tentative interpretation with unspecified abbreviation expansions and acknowledges excess freedom. Its Latin reading is unverified; it is not accepted here as a recovered deterministic key or a verified partial solution. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): the episode is Valladolid 1604, not 1599 (as Cryptiana noted). Valle never says he broke these letters: he says he already had 'la misma' cipher, shown to Philip II fifteen years earlier. The ciphertext is two real letters, to Andrés de Prada (f. 85r) and to Juan Baptista de Tassis (ff. 86r-86v), so Spanish or Italian rather than Latin. Unread; the BDH images (140 ppi) are too coarse, and he has asked the BNE for high-resolution scans. 28 Oct 2026 (targets/sirtori1604/, in progress): system narrowed from the 2012 transcriptions, nothing read. f. 85 has 94 space-separated groups of 1-4 signs (2.19 per group, 59% exactly 2), half the length of Spanish, Italian or Latin words, so not a letter-for-letter substitution; the lengths match Spanish syllables but no vowel set exists (64%, shuffled 60-63%, real syllables 89%); substitution annealing of the Gomez stream fails in es/it/la where same-length controls are recovered. Points to syllable or code signs with meaningful dots and commas; needs the high-resolution scans and Valle's ff. 83-84, 88-90.
entries.why: Sirtori's own cipher, and a test of the claim by Spain's cipher secretary that he had anticipated it.
entries.verify: Download ff. 83-90 from BDH, re-transcribe keeping the abbreviation marks, and test Caballero's partial key against a Latin (and Italian/Spanish) model; read ff. 83-84 and 88-90 for Valle's own description of the scheme.
entries.known: Broken at the time by Luis Valle de la Cerda (his solution not extant). Transcription by Sara Gómez Hernández; Eloy Caballero's tentative partial Latin reading (2012, Cipher Mysteries) is unverified and not accepted here.
entries.open: The ciphertext of ff. 85r, 86r-86v (747 signs in the 2012 stream): no key. Not a letter substitution of es/it/la (group lengths; controlled solver runs, targets/sirtori1604/). Needs a transcription keeping every dot, comma, arc and loop count from the high-resolution scans Dudout has ordered, and Valle's ff. 83-84, 88-90.

entries.title: Ferdinand, King of Hungary and Bohemia (future Ferdinand III), to Maximilian von Trauttmansdorff, letter in cipher
entries.correspondents: Ferdinand, King of Hungary and Bohemia (future Emperor Ferdinand III) → Maximilian von Trauttmansdorff
entries.shelfmark: SOA Plzeň, pracoviště Klášter u Nepomuka, Rodinný archiv Trauttmansdorffů, karton 6, inv. č. 68
entries.status: Attempted 26 Oct 2026 (ferdinand1634), closed unread: no image of the letter is online or in print. Mírka (2012, n. 37-39, 135): a contemporary copy, the only enciphered one among the copies of Ferdinand's letters to Trauttmansdorff; a clear note at the end says Ferdinand enciphered it and sent it by his own messenger; cipher alphabet of two- and three-digit numbers only (nomenclator with homophones, bigrams, probably codes). Not on DECODE.
entries.why: A ciphered letter from the victor of Nördlingen to the Emperor's chief negotiator in November 1634, during the Pirna talks that led to the Peace of Prague.
entries.verify: Order scans of kart. 6, inv. č. 68 from SOA Plzeň (Klášter). Mírka (n. 38) suggests the key may be in Vienna (FA Trauttmansdorff, HHStA). Not the R1887 system of 28 Oct 1634 (graphic signs + three-letter codes, ferdinand3).
entries.known: Mírka 2012 describes a numerical nomenclator (two- and three-digit numbers) that he could not break. Ferdinand's graphic-sign cipher of 28 Oct 1634 (R1887, ferdinand3) is a different system.
entries.open: The whole letter: not seen; no image online, on DECODE or in Mírka's article; scans needed from SOA Plzeň.

entries.folio_note: Deciphered at the time: Colbert 427 f. 325 (to Henri III, Fribourg, 23 Apr 1585; marginal decipherment), fr. 16026 f. 120, f. 126, p. 129. Michael Brackx's provisional transcription of f. 325 (issue #82 comment): about 244 signs, figures and invented symbols; a 17-sign glossed group on f. 325v gives a tentative homophonic partial key; a sliding test of that key on the main block was no better than chance.
entries.status: Reported by Michael Brackx (issue #82, 22 Oct 2026), from Rott, Inventaire sommaire I (1882) pp. 193–197. Rott marks only f. 99 and part of pp. 130–130bis 'non déchiffré'. Fr. 16026 is not digitised (Biblissima: numérisation indisponible); Colbert 427 is on Gallica. Rott vol. I could not be checked here (only the index volume is on archive.org; it confirms Fleury's embassy), and Gallica's bot check blocked a look at f. 325 on 22 Oct 2026. Not on DECODE or Cryptoole.
entries.why: French embassy to the Swiss under Henri III: a key that can be rebuilt from the online deciphered sibling, with four more deciphered letters in the same volume as the unread ones.
entries.verify: Transcribe Colbert 427 f. 325 at full resolution and align it with its marginal decipherment to rebuild the key; request photographs of fr. 16026 f. 99, f. 120, f. 126, pp. 129–130bis and apply it.
entries.known: Siblings deciphered at the time (Colbert 427 f. 325, fr. 16026 f. 120, f. 126, p. 129). Brackx's tentative partial key from the f. 325v name group (17 signs: messieurs de Surich).
entries.open: fr. 16026 f. 99 and the undeciphered part of pp. 130–130bis; the key itself is not yet rebuilt.

entries.title: Antoni Augustyn Deboli → King Stanisław August, cipher despatches from St Petersburg, 1784
entries.correspondents: Antoni Augustyn Deboli (Polish envoy at St Petersburg) → Stanisław August
entries.language: Polish/French (unknown which; the clear despatches of the same days are in Polish)
entries.shelfmark: AGAD Warszawa, Zbiór Popielów (zesp. 12), sygn. 10
entries.folio_note: 82 pieces, k. 272
entries.status: Existing for the despatches the cabinet register covers (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026), not yet matched piece by piece. The King's cabinet kept Deboli's despatches of 1784-85 in clear in AGAD, Archiwum Królestwa Polskiego (zesp. 11) 1/11/0/-/267, 'Deboli' 2 Jan 1784 - 20 Dec 1785 (790 scans). The King's drafts to Deboli for the same years are AKP 268 (419 scans), and AKP 264 has extracts, among them one of 20 Aug 1784. Unprinted: Zielińska & Danilczyk stop at 31 Dec 1782. Systems seen on the ZbPop 10 scans: the old Polish code (ZbPop 444) in 'Sire' despatches, and a second table with 2084, 1103 and 509 frequent (groups to about 3800, e.g. 2 Jul 1784), for which no key of the time was found; ZbPop 451 gives only French fragments on it. Keys of the time: ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska' of 8 Mar 1783 (1/12/0/-/444, 9 scans) is the old Polish code of 1783-88 (signal group 2345), not the 1789-91 code of targets/deboli1789; ZbPop 451 'Chiffre François Nouveau' of 1780 (1/12/0/-/451, 9 scans) is a French table. Both are online on szukajwarchiwach. We have transcribed both; the transcription will come with a later target. Earlier note: AGAD inventory: "Korespondencja polityczna tajna (pismo cyfrowe) ... Listy zapisane szyfrem"; no decipherment noted. Keys in the same fonds: ZbPop 444 "Cyfra polska posłana do Petersburga Deboliemu" 8 III 1783; 451 "Chiffre François Nouveau envoyé a Monsieur Deboli" 1780; 453-454 the Cabinet's numbered keys 1772-1795 (not seen online). Not on DECODE (list dump searched); not in repo (known.py Deboli, Popiel: no hits). No scan album found on agadd2 for this signature; may be on szukajwarchiwach (blocked).
entries.why: The Polish envoy's secret reports from Catherine II's court to the King; the ciphered parts carry what he would not put in the open despatch.
entries.score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Polish archives sweep (research/polish_archives/); not viewed
entries.verify: Check the open Polish despatch of the same date (ZbPop 419/420/421/417/415) and any cabinet decipherment; try the 1780 French key (ZbPop 451) and the 1783 Polish key (ZbPop 444) if obtainable; Zielińska's 1780-82 volumes give plaintext for code-group calibration.
entries.prior_art: open as far as checked: Zielińska & Danilczyk print the Deboli correspondence only for 1780, 1781, 1782 (IH PAN, 2015-2017+); later years unedited, Rolnik 2025 says the Great Sejm reports remain in manuscript. A contemporary decipherment may survive in the King's cabinet copies (cf. entries.folio_note: 223 images online (IIIF A0073297). Image 107: a full page of 3-digit numeric cipher (groups 17-720, dot-separated) facing a French clear page mentioning the Empress, Saldern; several more all-cipher pages around images 60-125 in a sampled contact sheet; images ~216-220 a folder "Chiffernycklar" and three key tables.

entries.title: Conrad Biermann's copybook, 1675: letters outside key K55
entries.correspondents: Danish German Chancery (Conrad Biermann) → Danish envoys abroad (Paris, The Hague, Stockholm, Hanover ...)
entries.shelfmark: Rigsarkivet, Tyske Kancelli, Udenrigske Afdeling, Almindelig del, "Conrad Biermanns kopibog over udgående skrivelser til danske ministre i udlandet" 1675 (Daisy heid 2130515, unit S-1418)
entries.folio_note: 255 images online (Arkivalieronline epid 15552891; image ids from 48573952). Image 109 (pp. 104-105): French letter with long runs of a numeric nomenclator (2-3 digit numbers 10-672) mixed with letters and symbols (X, #, pi-like signs), no interlinear decipherment.
entries.status: Daisy (new search): "En stor del af de indførte skrivelser er i chifre." Viewed one opening (image 109): ciphertext copied into the register, clear text around it, no decipherment. Not on DECODE, not in the repo. Key lead: Tyske Kancelli "Chiffer" 1670-1709 (heid 2132747, "a mix of many different cipher keys"), fully scanned (epid 15553654). 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): Copenhagen to Just Høeg at The Hague, 2, 5 and 9 January 1675, read: 841 of 849 groups, key = the untitled sheet at image 55 of the TKUA 'Chiffer' volume 1670-1709, checked on letters to Meyercrone in Paris in the same key. The rest of the copybook not reported. Extended 27 Oct 2026 (Europe chiffrée, documents.html#hoeg-1675, #meyercrone-1675): 37 letters read with key K55, 18 to Høeg (2 Jan-5 June 1675) and 19 to Meyercrone (16 Feb-21 June; 6,103 groups, 99.4%). Still open: the letters to Lilienkron (German, numbers 14-707 with the signs Δ θ), to Gioë and Schröder (K55 family, untested) and the letter of 2 Jan to Meyercrone (another key); see the survey in targets/biermann1675/. Merged 27 Oct 2026 (pull request #133): with the eleven Høeg letters of 2 Jan-9 Feb and the 23 March letter read in targets/biermann1675 on 26 Oct, every image-55 letter to Høeg and Meyercrone is now read there. Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
entries.why: Danish foreign policy at the start of the Scanian War (Gottorp, France, Sweden, Niels Brahe's mission) in the chancery's own outgoing ciphers; clear context and probable keys online.
entries.score_note: Scored from the Rigsarkivet description and one viewed opening during the Oct 2026 Rigsarkivet sweep (research/scandinavia/)
entries.verify: Test K55 on the Gioë and Schröder letters; look for the Lilienkron key and the 2 Jan Meyercrone key in TKUA "Chiffer" 1670-1709 (scanned).
entries.prior_art: partial: 37 letters to Høeg and Meyercron read with key K55 (Dudout, Europe chiffrée; targets/biermann1675); image 109 viewed 2 Nov 2026 with no decipherment on the leaf

entries.title: Wallis's 'challenge' letters nos. 50, 51 and 53
entries.correspondents: Henri Brasset → Antoine de Bordeaux-Neufville; George Villiers, 2nd Duke of Buckingham → unknown; Peter Townesend → unknown; unknown → unknown
entries.language: French (EMLO: 'not deciphered and is in French')
entries.shelfmark: Bodleian Library, MS. e Mus. 203 pp. 218-226; copies in MS. Eng. misc. e. 475 pp. 234-247 and 'MS. 19336' pp. 203-219 (EMLO's manifestation shelfmarks)
entries.folio_note: Letters 50-53 of Wallis's 'Collection of letters intercepted in cipher' (1653): no. 50 Brasset → Bordeaux 4 Apr 1653 (numeric + symbol substitution), no. 51 unknown, Scotland, 16 Jan 1651, no. 52 Buckingham, undated, no. 53 Peter Townesend, Flanders, 5 May 1658 (numeric substitution). EMLO works cb69093b, 3329a9ec, 86e81b88, eef01c0b.
entries.status: EMLO notes for each: 'The letter is not deciphered; however, the cipher appears to be based on the substitution of numeric values.' The auction copy of the same collection (Dominic Winter, 7 Oct 2020, lot 375) says the last four letters are 'left unsolved as exercises for aspirant cryptographers'. The other 49 letters carry Wallis's decipherment and key, so related Royalist/French keys sit in the same volume. Not on DECODE under these shelfmarks (known.py: no hit for e Musaeo 203 / Eng. misc. e. 475 / Brasset 1653; DECODE has a different Brasset record R9429, Oct 1648). frame_check.frame: APUG 563 f. 179v and f. 181r (crops on the Wuerzburg page, images botschaft_1a.jpg and botschaft_2.jpg)
frame_check.saw: Not the Gregorian repository viewer (EMLO page never loaded; archimede.imss.fi.it/kircher/563/large/ is 403 and the Stanford Luna Insight route is obsolete). I saw two crops of the cryptogram leaves reproduced by Vollrath (Wuerzburg), captioned Ausschnitte aus APUG 563 179v und 181r. 179v: a circle containing a 12x12 grid of the numbers 1-144 in scrambled order (41 80 11 74 12 90 ...), with a 4-line Latin instruction above in Kirchers hand (in quadrato hoc numeros continens ... ). 181r: a circle with a 12x12 grid of Latin syllables (vo tus sint ri prin quan to lu ...), a Latin note above (Jam hic secreta ex praecedenti tabula ...) and a tally of strokes with the number 35. So the cryptogram is a numbered square plus a syllable square, a key-and-message pair, in Latin. No decipherment written on them.
frame_check.note: Page text says the enigma was Kirchers own, sent to the duke, with the dukes receipt dated 29 Sept 1664 answering a letter of 31 Aug; so the cryptogram leaves ff.179-181 look like Kirchers enigma rather than a dukes cryptogram, and the 1 Jun 1664 letter ff.88r-89v was not viewed. Whole leaves not seen, only crops.

His stated convention is at vol 1 p. 237 n. 1 ('Die schräg gedruckten Stellen sind dechiffrirt'). OBA 21069 = no. 115 (vol 1 pp. 281-282, page image viewed): headed 'Orig. eighdg.' with no cipher note and no italics; the separate cipher Beibrief is not printed. OBA 21213 = no. 122 (DDB 'Druck: Joachim, Albrecht I Nr. 122'; pp. 289-290 viewed): regest plus long extracts headed 'Orig. — O. S.', no italics and no cipher note, so whether its cipher passages are among the printed extracts cannot be told. 22744 (D. 53, 23 Oct 1519) and 22849 (D. 529) are only cited in the vol 2 apparatus. 25970 is only cited in a vol 3 footnote ('in Chiffern. D. 87'), to a narrative sentence on Albrecht's plans, so Joachim knew its content, but prints no text. 25346 is only cited, from register copy 'Reg. A. 184 fol. 44 v', which may be a clear copy; not online. DDB shows a 'Druck' note only for 21069 and 21213.

entries.title: Lic. Melchior (Vienna, Prague, Strasbourg) and the envoys Pape and Köhler → Count Wolfgang Julius of Hohenlohe, partly ciphered reports with key
entries.correspondents: Lic. Melchior; Johann Christoph Pape and Georg Ludwig Köhler → Wolfgang Julius of Hohenlohe-Neuenstein
entries.shelfmark: Landesarchiv BW, Hohenlohe-Zentralarchiv Neuenstein, Sf 35 Bü 161 and 165 (key Bü 226)
entries.folio_note: Bue 161 (1679-80, Melchior; 'Beilage: Chiffrierschluessel') and Bue 165 (1689, Pape and Koehler, servants sent to Vienna on house business; the finding aid says 'teilweise chiffriert', not a diplomatic mission)
entries.status: Not the key to these letters; both files existing in part (issue #254). Bü 226 ('Clavis zu der Ochsischen Correspondenz') is a complete key for a different affair, the Ochs case before an imperial court: alphabet 1-60 in sequence, nomenclator 61-167. It fits neither Bü 161 nor Bü 165. Bü 161 (Lic. Melchior, Vienna, March-May 1679, Reichshofrat case) uses a 3-digit nomenclator plus a 2-digit homophonic alphabet. The 'Beilage' is a set of contemporary decipherment sheets, and the letter of 21/31 May 1679 is fully deciphered by one of them (existing). Three other letters (a copy, 23 Mar/2 Apr and 27 Mar/6 Apr 1679) use the same nomenclator but have no contemporary solution in the scans we have; our attempt on them did not validate (0.79 against a 0.85 threshold). Bü 165 (Pape/Köhler, Vienna, Jan-Mar 1689) is a different system with a contemporary interlinear decipherment (existing). Dates: 1679 and 1689, not 1678-1689. Earlier note: Finding aid as quoted; listed but not rowed in research/central_archives. Not digitised.
entries.why: A count's agents at the imperial court in the Dutch War years. Follow-up (issue #254): the open part is the three Bü 161 letters of March-April 1679, in the same nomenclator as the deciphered letter of 21/31 May 1679; Bü 226 is not their key.

entries.status: Identified 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #101; targets/puebla1495/): the cipher copy of the despatch of 28 Dec 1495 whose clear draft Bergenroth abstracted in CSP Spain I no. 113 (no. 114 notices the cipher copy, 'substance exactly the same', with no decipherment); five sending dates on p. 2 match no. 113 and no other item. A sample (p. 1 ll. 6-8) decoded with the extant key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33. Open: the cipher copy beyond the sample, and the groups 883, 1374, 1335, 1813, 852, 868, 1221 and 'xxix' (key images not opened: PARES HTTP 429). No page.
entries.why: Anglo-Spanish diplomacy of 1495 (Perkin Warbeck, the Catherine of Aragon marriage treaty) in a code whose 2400-element key survives.
entries.score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 PARES sweep (research/pares_ags/); not viewed
entries.verify: Decode the rest of pp. 1-4 with the PTR 52 doc. 33 key (key images 3-9, 47-51, 70-75, 78-84, 110-113 for the open groups) and compare the wording with no. 113.
entries.prior_art: checked 27 Oct 2026: content in print as Bergenroth's abstract of the clear draft (CSP Spain I no. 113, pp. 72-75); no decipherment of the cipher copy printed (no. 114); 1868 Supplement starts in 1498

frame_check.saw: Image 1: about 27 lines of Roman-numeral cipher (dar + lxxi style numerals with strokes/abbreviation marks, interspersed with some clear Spanish words e.g. names Diego de Soria, John de Santangel), docket "De los Reyes cifra sin fecha", old mark T.C.Y.2. Image 2: about 25 lines, same Roman-numeral cipher with a few plain words (Salvador Duarte, la compania). No decipherment written on either page. Spanish. 4 images total (664R-665V); only images 1-2 viewed.

entries.vetting_note: Unopened editions that would cover the unread part: Antonio de la Torre, Documentos sobre relaciones internacionales de los Reyes Catolicos vol. V (1495-1497, CSIC 1965), and Suarez Fernandez, Politica internacional de Isabel la Catolica vol. IV (1972). Neither is on archive.org (advancedsearch 0 hits); Google Books gives the set no preview or snippet only, and searches there for the despatch returned nothing either way. Either may print the clear draft of 28 Dec 1495 in full, so the prior-art question is unanswered. Opened: CSP Spain I pp. 72-79 (BHO in Chrome): no. 113 is an English abstract of the draft with quotations, no. 114 notices the cipher copy ('Written in two different keys of cipher, one of which is extant') with no decipherment. Tomokiyo, spanish.htm: lists PTR 52 doc. 124 as 'another undated letter' in a list of letters probably using the code, with no reading. Not checked: Rymer, Rodriguez Villa, Mattingly (no text opened; none is known to print this despatch). New for whoever resumes: CSP no. 117 (pp. 75-77), the merchant-cover letter of the same day from 'MCCCIX (Guide)' to Alonzo de Compludo, also names Diego de Soria, Juan de Santa Gadea and the Company, and Bergenroth prints its groups deciphered. Doc. 124 uses the same cover words, so compare doc. 124 with no. 117 as well as no. 113: the identification with no. 113 alone is not settled. If de la Torre V and Suarez IV show no print, the block can be open with key_held AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33.

seen.extent: 4 images (pp. 1-4, foliation 664-665): image 1 about 27 lines and image 2 about 25 lines of Roman-numeral groups; image 4 a further full page of about 28 lines (image 3 not opened). Spanish. Cipher copy of the Ferdinand and Isabella despatch to De Puebla of 28 Dec 1495.
seen.cipher: Dense lines of Roman numerals in script forms (da/dar/jV ligatures, strokes and abbreviation marks) with a few clear names (Diego de Soria, Iohn de Santagadea, Diego Lopez de Ayala, Salvador Duarte); docket 'De los Reyes cifra sin fecha', old mark T.C.Y. 2. Nothing is written between the lines or on the leaves as a decipherment. Image 4 carries a modern note that targets/puebla1495/NOTES.md reads as 'Carta de los RR.CC. al doctor Puebla en cifra incompleta' (a description, not a reading).

prior_art.tomokiyo: cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/spanish.htm (fetched 4 Nov 2026): describes Puebla's Great Roman Numeral Code (2400 elements, key PTR,LEG,52,DOC.33) and lists PTR,LEG,52,DOC.124 as 'another undated letter ... from 1495' probably in that code; no reading given. Not on unsolved.htm.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry or HistoCrypt paper on the Puebla code or on doc. 124 found: GL.htm grepped (no Simancas/Puebla entry) and web search 'Puebla Great Roman Numeral Code Lasry HistoCrypt Cryptologia' returned only unrelated 2018 CNI Great Captain news.
prior_art.edition: Bergenroth, CSP Spain I (1862) no. 113 pp. 72-75 prints an abstract of the clear draft; no. 114 p. 75 (BHO pp72-79, fetched 4 Nov 2026) reads 'The same despatch written in cipher ... Written in two different keys of cipher, one of which is extant' and prints no decipherment of the cipher copy. De la Torre, Documentos sobre relaciones internacionales de los Reyes Catolicos V (1965) and Suarez Fernandez IV (1972) not opened (not online); Galende Diaz's study of the Puebla cipher (Univ. Granada, digibug 10481/30410) describes the code, not this despatch.
prior_art.literature: Web searches (Puebla cipher Roman numerals decipherment; Galende Diaz La escritura cifrada durante el reinado de los Reyes Catolicos) found descriptions of the 2400-word code, no published reading of doc. 124. Project notes (targets/puebla1495) record a sample decode p. 1 ll. 6-8 and p. 2 ll. 1-2 with the extant key, made 27 Oct 2026 by WAINUT; that is our own partial work, not prior art in print.

vetting.key_check: The extant key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33 (PARES show/2207755) is held and was applied to a 3-line sample (targets/puebla1495) which gives coherent Spanish; the rest of the cipher copy is not decoded and eight groups (883, 1374, 1335, 1813, 852, 868, 1221, 'xxix') lack values. Bergenroth says the despatch exists in two keys, so the second key is not held. The key does not close the lead because no reading beyond the sample is on record.

entries.title: French consular dispatches in cipher to Talleyrand captured on the ship Astrea (the Gibraltar packet)
entries.correspondents: J. A. B. Rozier (former French vice consul at New York) → Talleyrand
entries.place: United States → Paris (captured at sea; sent on by US consul John Gavino, Gibraltar)
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Miscellaneous Letters of the Department of State (M179 roll 17): John Adams to Timothy Pickering, Quincy, 1 Apr 1799 (naId 55028996), the cover letter; the location of the ciphered packet itself (originals and the Adams copies by Thomas B. Adams and William Shaw) is not established
entries.folio_note: Adams's cover letter is not digitised in the catalogue; the packet held at least two letters from Rozier (Brumaire and Frimaire an VII) plus others; length unknown
entries.status: NARA item description: Adams submits 'a packet of papers sent by the United States Consul at Gibraltar, but they have not been deciphered'. Adams's letter (Founders Online) says no one in Boston would undertake them and James Lovell 'despairs of being able to make a key'. Pickering to Hamilton 18 Jun 1799: Rozier showed his cipher and Pickering checked some coded passages against Rozier's plain copies. So the Rozier letters were checked in part with the writer's own key; the other letters in the packet and a full decipherment are not recorded. Not on DECODE; not in the repo. 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #110; targets/astrea1799/, in progress): the editors name only the two Rozier letters as in code (no. 1, 27 Oct 1798; no. 2, 22 Nov 1798 with a postscript of 23 Nov and an extract of Rozier to Hédouville of 20 Nov). Pickering's check-reading (PAH 23:199-200) is a summary only; no decipherment in print. Adams Papers microfilm reel 393 at MHS (slip 100399, 32 p.) holds the packet or the Adams copies.
entries.why: French consular reporting to Talleyrand at the height of the Quasi-War, read by the Adams administration only through the writer's own selective key demonstration.

entries.status: Weber (Masked Dispatches, 3rd ed. 2013, pp. 114-116 and n. 63): Keefer 'could not decipher it' and hoped for the plain text from a French newspaper; 'There is no evidence Keefer ever solved the French cipher.' entries.title: Joel Roberts Poinsett → James Monroe, Santiago de Chile, despatch with at least nine cipher passages printed as '(undeciphered cipher)'
entries.correspondents: Joel Roberts Poinsett (US special agent and consul general for Buenos Aires, Chile and Peru) → James Monroe, Secretary of State
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from Special Agents, vol. 3 (Poinsett 1813-23) = microfilm M37 roll 2, catalog naId 213803757; Poinsett's other 1811-14 reports ('parts in cipher') are in the Poinsett Papers vol. 4, Historical Society of Pennsylvania (Gilpin collection)
entries.folio_note: nine '(undeciphered cipher)' insertions in Manning's text, single words to whole clauses (on the Carreras, the Buenos Aires army, the Portuguese, the Araucanian chief); frame of the letter not located (M37 roll 2 frames 16-24 are the Poinsett list and his 'State of society' essay) Frame located 27 Oct 2026 (research/nara_triage_a/): M37 roll 2, frame 0093; a coded sibling of 14 June 1814 is at frames 0097-0099.
entries.status: Manning 1925 vol. 2, doc. 442, pp. 896-897, prints the despatch with '(undeciphered cipher)' at each coded passage; the State Department returned Poinsett's other letters to him in 1818, so his own copies (some 'Part in cipher', May-July 1811 from Buenos Aires, per the HSP list filmed at M37 roll 2 frames 20-22) are at HSP, possibly with plaintext drafts. Not in the repo (known.py: Poinsett no hits). Worked 28 Oct 2026 (targets/poinsett1813, write-up poinsett1813): 437 groups transcribed; the same-code letter of 14 June 1814 (no. 651) carries a clerk's decipherment, 95 values, 161 of 437 groups of 1813 get a value, no sentence reads. Other State Department rolls searched (M37 1-2, M70, M77, M84): no further letter in the code.

entries.title: Delacroix (French Foreign Minister) → Létombe (French consul general, Philadelphia), despatch No. 5 entirely in a French numeric code, copy sent by Rufus King
entries.correspondents: Charles Delacroix → Philippe de Létombe (copy forwarded by Rufus King to Timothy Pickering)
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Great Britain, vol. 5 (10 Aug 1796-28 Dec 1797) = microfilm M30 roll 4 (image path M30-004), catalog naId 188512917
entries.folio_note: frames 0244 right, 0245 left and right (0244 left blank): 653 code groups, values 2-1198, 297 distinct, in a clerk's copy marked 'Dup.', '(Copy)', 'No. 5 Duplicata'; heading and close in clear, signed 'Ch. Delacroix'; catchwords (806, 278) at the page feet confirm no group lost between pages. King's covering No. 53 ends on frame 0243.
entries.status: Transcribed in full by Michael Brackx (issue #122, 27 Oct 2026; transcription in the issue). King's No. 53: 'I have no means of decyphering it'; no decipherment on frames 0236-0252. Turner, Correspondence of the French Ministers 1791-1797 (AHA 1903) does not print No. 5, but prints Létombe's reply No. 42 (22 Brumaire an VI, p. 1077, from the ministry's decipherment, CP États-Unis 48 f. 355): he will follow what the 25 Messidor despatch prescribed for keeping his political correspondence, 'dont je dicte moi-même les chiffres'. So part of No. 5 is probably about the keeping and ciphering of his political letters. Statistics: repeats 705 806 711/400 405 ×7, 474 670 1068 ×3; adjacent frequent pairs 972/973 and 81/82 hint at a one-part code, but a one-part word anneal did not converge; flat profile (top ten 14%). Not on DECODE. 2 Nov 2026: worked in targets/delacroix1797/, still unread. Near-repeated passages interchange neighbouring numbers (e.g. 417 269/416 268, 123 151/124 152), which suggests homophones in small numeric blocks, and a calibrated one-part test found no alphabetical order (real text overlaps scrambled numbers; the method recovers about half of a synthetic one-part letter). Annealers failed calibration on synthetic letters of the same size; seven French keys in the repo are within chance.
entries.why: A Directory instruction to the French chargé/consul general in Philadelphia days before Delacroix left office and on the eve of the XYZ mission, which Rufus King obtained in London (probably from Grenville's decipherers); its content is not known from the US side.
entries.verify: Find the clear minute of 25 Messidor an V in AMAE CP États-Unis 47 or 48, or Nasatir & Monell's calendar (1967). Alternatively, find Létombe's 1797-98 ciphered despatches with the ministry's decipherments (CP États-Unis 48; Turner prints them from the decipherment) to rebuild the code. New lead: CADN Nantes, Philadelphia consulate 519PO/1 art. 1 (ministry letters received, March 1793-Feb 1798).

entries.title: Bernstorff (German Embassy Washington), second code text on the State Department cable of 11 Jan 1917 (groups 147-576), unread
entries.correspondents: Count Johann Heinrich von Bernstorff → Auswärtiges Amt, Berlin (via Secretary Lansing and Amembassy Berlin)
entries.folio_note: Roll 166 frames 0785-0786 (sheets 1 and 2; 0786 is not reversed): 577 groups in all (505 four-figure, 67 five-figure, 4 three-figure, 1 six-figure). Groups 0-146 are telegram No. 205; groups 147-576 are a second text in the same code.
entries.status: 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #115; targets/bernstorff1917/): groups 0-146 are Bernstorff's telegram No. 205 of 10 Jan 1917, printed by Bernstorff (1920, pp. 325-326) and in Official German Documents II p. 1017; aligning them gave 82 groups of a two-part four-figure code with prefix figures (not 13040; probably 0075 [?]). Written up. The memorandum on frames 0769-0775 is not the plaintext. This entry is now the second text, 430 groups in the same code, unread. 2 Nov 2026 (section 10 of the notes): the code is Code 7500 of Friedman and Mendelsohn 1938 by route and structure (this cable not named there); their nine sibling telegrams were not found on the digitised reels; catalogue 635 keeps no groups; the text is not in Bernstorff 1920 or Official German Documents. A crib needs PA AA, TNA HW 7/ADM 137, or State Department files on site.
entries.why: A German Embassy code telegram of the last weeks before unrestricted U-boat warfare, with a near-certain crib; a test of the 13040/0075 codes on known text.

entries.title: German Minister at Lima: batches London could not decipher, and the Quito-Lima letter code
entries.correspondents: German Legation Lima (Minister Perl; later Weyers) ↔ German legations in Santiago, Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Mexico
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Central Decimal File 1910-29, 862.20223 (German military activities in Peru), sub-nos. 4-99
entries.folio_note: The 862.20223 file is scanned: M336 roll 64 (RG 64 copy, item naId 574876562), frames c. 0048-0207 and later (found 27 Oct 2026 in the NARA bulk sweep, slice J). It holds the US Legation's relays of the German code telegrams (5-figure groups), a letter code between Quito and Lima (f.0104), the Department's re-sends 'For Bell from Harrison' (f.0049-0054, 0069, 0103, 0129-0132, 0204), London's replies (f.0101 'Second undecipherable ... Fourth undecipherable'; f.0207 a verbatim English text), Lima's despatch of 6 June 1917 (f.0070-0072) and Handley's of 9 Oct 1917 (f.0205). Purport list: M973 roll 207 frames 1008-1014.
entries.status: Partially read at the time: London (Bell / Gunther, i.e. Room 40 via the US Embassy) cabled back the 'substance' of most batches; Lima 85 (9 Oct 1917) reports some messages could not be deciphered. entries.title: Soviet and German cipher radiograms of 1921 (Moscow ↔ Berlin, Stockholm, Christiania, Kharkov), intercepted at Constantinople by the US High Commission and never deciphered
entries.correspondents: Chicherin / Narkomindel Moscow ↔ Soviet representation Berlin (Kopp, Krestinsky, 'Polpred'), Stockholm, Christiania, Reval; Nikolaev → Kharkov; Auswärtiges Amt Berlin ↔ Deutsche Vertretung Moskau (Hilger); copies sent by Admiral Mark L. Bristol, US High Commissioner, Constantinople
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Central Decimal File 1910-29, 861.00 (Political Affairs, Russia), microfilm M316 rolls 40-48 (RG 64 digital copies): file units naId 604700562 (861.00/8376-8492, Mar 1921), 604701877 (8493-8622, Apr), 604703234 (8623-8773, May-Jun), 604704577 (8774-8910, Jun-Jul), 604705830 (8911-9012, Jul-Sep), 604707113 (9013-9064, Sep-Oct), 604708415 (9065-9159, Oct-Nov), 604709981 (9160-9240, Nov-Dec), 604711297 (9241-9329, Dec 1921-Feb 1922); the War Department copies are RG 457, Archival and Historian's Source Files, 6707N 'Russian Coded Messages, 1921 (Provided by U.S. High Commissioner Constantinople)' (naId 23890165, not digitised)
entries.folio_note: Typed copies of intercepted radiograms, one per frame with date, route and addresses (e.g. 'MARCH 22d 1921 FROM ... TO MOSCOW 71915 67404 33684 ...'; 'SEPTEMBER 4th 1921 FROM BERLIN TO MOSCOW SCHITSCHERIN MOSKAU FUNKSPRUCH'; 'SEPTEMBER 28th 1921 FROM MOSCOW TO BERLIN POLPRED BERLIN'), mostly 4- and 5-figure groups. Frames with cipher text by roll (OCR count): M316-040 0889-0893 (5); 041 0543-1068 (61); 042 0244-1276 (83); 043 0427-1204 (42); 044 0186-1073 (56); 045 0048-0638 (22); 046 0178-1178 (45); 047 0155-1070 (64); 048 0128-0766 (13): about 390 frames, about 62,000 groups. Covering despatches: 861.00/8575 (Bristol No. 153, 20 Apr 1921, M316-041-0871: the Russian intercept operator's notes on the traffic), 040-0888 (March 1921: hopes anti-Bolshevik Russians may help find the key; Col. Castle sending similar messages to the War Department), 043-0936 (July 1921: 'unable to report any progress regarding the deciphering of the code messages of the Bolshevik Government'); 9071, 9130, 9132, 9133 (Oct-Nov 1921, Moscow-Berlin and Moscow-Christiania). M316-041-1073 'Deciphered telegrams of Soviet authorities' (Petrograd-Reval) is a separate, small set in clear.
entries.status: Unblocked 27 Oct 2026 (NARA slice L, research/nara_triage_l/): the purport list (naId 87657409) led to the 861.00 file, which is filmed on M316 and digitised as RG 64 copies; all nine 1921 rolls fetched and the OCR read. The High Commission could not decipher the traffic and the Department records no decipherment; the War Department (MI-8) received parallel copies (RG 457 6707N). Some of the same Soviet traffic may have been read by GC&CS (HW 12, 1921) and the German side is Auswärtiges Amt traffic; neither has been checked. Distinct from 710 (Chicherin → Sukhanov 1918). Worked 2 Nov 2026. Letter traffic in the file is a columnar transposition with a key per telegram: two deciphered and removed from this entry's open work (targets/lejava1921/, targets/voikov1921/); others in targets/voikov1921b/, targets/stomoniakov1921/. Figure traffic, the core of this entry, still unread: no group value recovered (targets/kopp1921/, targets/karakhan1921/). HW 12 and RG 457 still unchecked.
entries.why: A large, dated corpus of early Soviet and German diplomatic cipher radio traffic from 1921, filed as typed copies with the intercept operator's notes: the Rapallo-era Moscow-Berlin channel, unread by the Americans who collected it.
entries.verify: View sample frames (M316-041-0543, 0871; 046-0178); separate the Russian and German systems by route and group length; check HW 12 (GC&CS) 1921 Soviet decrypts and the RG 457 4896 worksheets for keys or matching texts; compare with TICOM 1036 on early Soviet systems.

entries.title: Richard Taylor's telegram letter-books 1865 (NARA RG 109 ch. II vols. 196, 11, 10): the cipher telegrams still unread and not in the Official Records
entries.correspondents: Richard Taylor (by W. F. Bullock Jr., AAG) → D. H. Maury (Mobile), S. D. Lee (Augusta), Wirt Adams, Gov. Clark, Richmond and others
entries.shelfmark: NARA RG 109, War Department Collection of Confederate Records, Chapter II vols. 10, 11 and 196 (Telegrams Sent, Department of Alabama, Mississippi and East Louisiana, 1864-1865)
entries.folio_note: Open: vol. 196 fr. 0030, 0032, 0053, 0056, 0064, 0065, 0071; vol. 11 fr. 0044 first passage, 0045, 0046; vol. 10 fr. 0056 provisional. Other runs in the OCR list were not image-checked and some are noise. Printed in OR: vol. 196 fr. 0010, 0022, 0027; vol. 11 fr. 0036, 0039, 0041, 0044 second, 0076-0077; vol. 10 fr. 0049, 0054. Read here, not found in OR: vol. 196 fr. 0018, 0031, 0052, 0055, 0061; vol. 11 fr. 0022. Correction: targets/taylor1865/NOTES.md says fr. 0027 has no cipher words; it holds Taylor to Brent, 17 Feb 1865, with long cipher runs.
entries.status: Narrowed 3 Nov 2026: read here or printed in OR are listed in folio_note; open are about ten telegrams of Feb-Apr 1865; held keys not yet run on them.
entries.why: A set of Confederate field ciphers from the last months of the war (Mobile campaign, Wilson's raid) that a known key reads, with the clear sense of each telegram in the same book: a quick, verifiable reading and a test set for Confederate key usage (which key, and when the change was made).
entries.score_note: Scored from NARA OCR and one viewed frame during the Oct 2026 NARA bulk-scan triage (research/nara_triage_d/)

entries.title: Russian Foreign Ministry bigram circulars to the New York consulate, 1891-97
entries.correspondents: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, St Petersburg (I Expédition / First Department; Obolensky, Shishkin as Adjoint) → Russian Consul General, New York (Olarovsky, Lodyzhensky)
entries.language: Russian or French (cover text French; plaintext unknown)
entries.shelfmark: NARA, RG 64 (microfilm M1486, Records of the Russian Consulates in the U.S., 1862-1922), roll 83, target 2 "Cables and Coded Communications, 1893-1910" (original: Russian Consulate New York, box 124); file unit naId 571170362
entries.folio_note: Roll 83 frames 0692-1550 (target 2 starts at frame 0692). Ciphertext circulars in 2-digit bigram-key groups: f.0696-0697 (15 Dec 1906), 0698 (10 Mar 1910, No. 63637), 0712 (18 Jun 1902, No. 281), 0732 (1895, No. 4945), 0742-0743 (No. 416), 0749 (1891, No. 3313), 0751-0752 (13 Aug 1891, No. 3902, c. 330 groups, viewed: clean, no interlinear), 0755-0757 (22 Mar 1895, No. 5078), 0769-0770 (10 Mar 1895, No. 5015), 0774 (31 Dec 1904, No. 1201), 0818-0820 (May/Jul 1897, Nos. 5657, 5700), 0823, 0835-0836, 0842, 0847, 0849; the consulate's replies in cipher f.0733-0735 (No. 519, 1895, Olarovsky); 5-digit secret circular No. 864 "aux Ambassades, Légations, Consulats" f.0703-0705 (c. 350 groups, viewed: clean, groups split by hand into 3-figure parts); 5-digit cables f.0694 (cable No. 63, 22 Oct 1908), 0800-0801, 0880-0882 (Oustinoff); naval-ministry letter cipher f.0805-0807 (5-letter groups with a repeating 2849284928... key line and Russian clear text: decrypted). Key material on the same roll: instructions and worked examples for the bigram keys No. 381 (1893; f.0780-0793) and No. 389 (1900; f.0713-0727, with the 12 Dec 1865 "Pesth" example in plaintext, transposition sheet and cipher), circular on key No. 400 (1905; f.0731), additions to the dictionary key No. 402 (1910; f.0728, 0802-0803), lozungi to recipher key No. 448 "Lambda" (1915; f.0869), rules on keeping keys (f.0759-0764), Naval Ministry cipher No. 383 (f.0863-0865) and Naval key No. 394 instructions plus dictionary (f.0884-0900, 0928-1073), and decode tables (f.1088-1550, "Разборная таблица No. 404" f.1443).
entries.status: Found in the RG 64 bulk_all hits (frames with 2-digit groups in a Russian consulate file); full roll OCR read and two frames viewed (0703, 0751). Some circulars carry the consulate's letter-by-letter decipherment worksheets on the following frames (f.0706-0711 after No. 864; 0758, 0772, 0776, 0794-0796, 0822-0825, 0837), so part of the run was read at the time; others show no worksheet in the OCR of the adjacent frames (1891 No. 3902, 1895 Nos. 4945 and 5078, 1906, 1910). The cipher system is described in full on the roll (bigram table + transposition "transparents" Lit. A/B/D; 3-figure values regrouped in 5s for the telegraph), and keys 381/389 come with plaintext-ciphertext examples. Not on DECODE; known.py: no hit for M1486, Olarovsky, Russian Consulate. Not in catalogue.json or any nara_* folder. || Brackx, issue #167 (28 Oct 2026): M1486 roll 83 (target 2, frames 0692-1550): the system is a bigram-table scheme (stencils A and D; instructions to keys 381 and 389, worked example 0790-0792); only key No. 404's tables are filmed (frames 1440-1446), so the 1888-1905 circulars' keys 356, 375, 381, 389 are not filmed; later circulars were deciphered at the time. Not checked on the film here. Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
entries.why: A run of tsarist Foreign Ministry cipher circulars to a consulate, filed with the consulate's own key instructions and worksheets: rare primary evidence of Russian diplomatic bigram ciphers and naval codes of 1890-1910, and the unread circulars can be tested against keys and worked examples on the same roll.

entries.title: Coahuila state code telegrams on the Mexican Kickapoo affair, Múzquiz ↔ Saltillo, 1906: two-digit code passages that the Mexican Embassy could not decipher
entries.correspondents: L. A. Guajardo (Jefe Político, Múzquiz) and Judge F. Valdés Llano → Governor Miguel Cárdenas, Saltillo; Cárdenas → Guajardo; R. C. Conine → Guajardo; Guajardo → Ignacio E. Rivas
entries.language: Spanish (clear passages translated into English for the Senate)
entries.shelfmark: NARA, RG 59, Numerical File 1906-1910, case 3706/35-45 (Kickapoo Indians), microfilm M862 roll 342; file unit naId 19505183
entries.folio_note: M862 roll 342 f.0500-0504 (Teller's letter of 8 Nov 1907 from Douglas, Arizona, enclosing the telegrams for deciphering, and the Department's memoranda); f.0505-0513 (copies of the telegrams numbered 35-45: 25 June, 30 June (2), 2 July, 11 July, 17 July, 19 July and Sabinas 27 July 1906; code passages as runs of two-digit numbers inside clear Spanish/English text, e.g. 'Conviene 70 48 35 40 34 30 98 99 70 90 73 49 ...'; c. 270 groups in the OCR, perhaps 400-450 on the frames); f.0514-0517 (Root's telegram and letter to Teller, 14 Nov 1907: 'The Mexican Embassy here does not know the code and is unable to decipher it').
entries.status: Found in the slice L word-hit triage of RG 59 (research/nara_triage_l/agent_59.md); the reel OCR was read again here (27 Oct 2026). The Senate subcommittee on the Mexican Kickapoo land frauds (Teller) obtained copies from the Federal telegraph office at Múzquiz and asked the Department for a decipherment; the Mexican Embassy could not read the code, suggested a state governors' code, and the copies were returned to Teller. Nothing later on the roll deciphers them. Repeated numbers inside words (10 35 30 18 / 10 35 70 18) and code mixed into clear text suggest a simple two-digit letter or syllable substitution with Spanish plaintext. known.py: no hits for Kickapoo, Múzquiz, Guajardo; not in catalogue.json.
entries.why: A Mexican state governor's telegraph code of 1906, unread by the Mexican Embassy and the State Department, filed with the clear context of a US Senate investigation into Kickapoo land frauds; likely readable from the ciphertext alone.
entries.score_note: Scored from the reel OCR during the Oct 2026 NARA caps/word rerun of the early groups (research/nara_triage_l/); frames not yet viewed

entries.status: Swept 28 Oct 2026 (Brice Dudout's PARES sweep, facet filter idFI); "cifrada", 17th century: "Minuta de despacho cifrada a Juan de Velasco y la Cueva, conde de Siruela". Sibling of the Genoa 1638-51 row already in the catalogue (Velasco y la Cueva, Eraso…), which may give the key family. Corrected 28 Oct 2026 after a full transcription (64 lines, 1,818 tokens): not a minute with clear passages but a despatch entirely in cipher (only the address in clear), dated 20 Nov 1638, in the Genoa 1638 system (genes1638 key family) with extra chancery signs (ℰ, ꝓ, ʒ, underlined sigla). Key K3k, trained on declared pairs in the same chancery hand (3594,149↔148, 158↔157, 160↔159, 151↔150 pp. 1-2, 3595,308↔309), frozen, then tested on 3594,151 image 3 ↔ 150 never seen: 0.888 of characters / 0.812 of words (normalised spelling; 200 controls p99 0.313 / 0.161), validated. Reading of 312: 884 words, about 87-88 % read by sense (61 unresolved, 57 restored, 8 probable), below the 95 % rule; what remains is the nomenclator (44 codes), not the signs. Subject: the negotiation with Genoa (passes, exchange of prisoners, galleys), answering Siruela's letters of 4 and 20 Oct 1638. Reported by Brice Dudout from his own look at the images; not yet checked here.

entries.title: Riverbank Laboratories 'Mexican codes' and unsorted cryptographic papers (the surviving Riverbank Department of Ciphers files)
entries.correspondents: Mexican government / agents (intercepted) -> Riverbank Department of Ciphers (W. F. and E. S. Friedman) for the State, War, Navy and Justice Departments
entries.shelfmark: New York Public Library, Manuscripts and Archives Division, MssCol 176 (Bacon cipher collection), box 15 'Riverbank Labs -- student exercises and lessons, Mexican codes' and box 16 'Riverbank Labs -- unsorted material concerning cryptography'
entries.folio_note: Box-level description only (1982 accession sheet, 33 boxes). Not digitised (NYPL Digital Collections shows 10 Baconian items only). Contents unknown: could be worksheets, intercept copies or training exercises built from them.
entries.status: Friedman's own accounts (NSA Friedman papers, folders 433/513) say Riverbank worked codes and ciphers forwarded by State, War, Navy and Justice in 1916-20; a 1917 Army note quoted in a web search summary says the main work was Mexican messages (source PDF not opened). Friedman wrote in 1948 that the Riverbank cipher records were thought destroyed after Fabyan's death (Cora Tyzzer letter, NSA A69876) and that the LoC Fabyan collection held none of them; the NYPL boxes came via Fabyan's widow to George Curtis (gift 1960), so these two boxes may be the only survivors. MI-8 broke several Mexican government codes in 1917-19 (repo: research/nara_triage_c/e), so many messages will be read; whether any are unread is unknown. Schmeh (2018) saw three boxes, not these. NSA historians (Dave Hatch and a colleague, a November visit, year not given) went through all nine Riverbank boxes and found them 'very duplicative and mixed': page proofs of Riverbank publications, student folders and exercises on graph paper, a few Parker Hitt letters; no cipher intercepts are mentioned (NSA blog 'A great TDY', Doc ID 6919113, released 30 Mar 2026).
entries.why: The only known surviving working files of the first US government cryptanalytic unit (Riverbank 1917-18); any message they hold unread is WWI German-Mexican traffic.
entries.score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Riverbank sweep (research/chi_riverbank/); not viewed
entries.verify: Request boxes 15 and 16 of MssCol 176 (NYPL Brooke Russell Astor Reading Room, appointment); list each cipher text and whether a solution sheet is with it; compare with the MID 10020 Riverbank monthly 'undeciphered messages' reports (catalogue 674).

entries.shelfmark: Bodleian Clarendon MS 63 ff. 33-4; cal. SP Dom 1658-9 p. 346; Cypher Collections vol. VI no. 35g (key from interlined decyphers)
entries.folio_note: Several short letters
entries.status: CSP Domestic notes say "a key to the cypher has been formed from decyphers interlined"; remaining figures not read.
entries.why: Intercepted correspondence on Richard Cromwell's fall.
entries.score_note: Scored from a printed calendar/edition note on archive.org during the Oct 2026 Internet Archive metadata sweep (research/ia_meta/); original manuscript not viewed
entries.verify: Fetch the Cypher Collections key; read the leftover groups.
entries.prior_art: open (checked 28 Oct 2026: known.py, DECODE list; calendar note only, no web search)

seen.where: archive.org OCR full text (djvu.txt) of the printed calendar, read in context on 29 Oct 2026: Calendar of the Clarendon State Papers vol. IV (Routledge 1932; archive.org calendarofclaren04bodluoft) and CSP Domestic 1658-9 (cu31924091770473).
seen.extent: Several short French letters (calendar says 'partly in cipher not deciphered'; the CSP Dom. 1658-9 copy of one is a 1.5-page letter 'all in Italics, cypher, undecyphered'); Marces made all copies.
seen.cipher: Clarendon IV: 'May 12/22 [De Vaux to Du Chastel] ... Intercepted letter; copy by Marces. (571.) Partly in cipher not deciphered. Cal. S.P. Dom., 1658-9, p. 346.' Also 'Apr. 23/May 3, Paris. Du Chastel to De Vaux ... All names are in cipher, but Marces subjoins a key (426) to some of those contained in letters between these two writers.' No full decipherment is written with the May or July copies.

prior_art.decode: Repo DECODE dumps and ledgers searched with known.py (29 Oct 2026) for the correspondents and shelfmark: no record; a calendar entry only, not on DECODE. Searched Marces, Du Chastel, Vaux: nothing.
prior_art.tomokiyo: No Tomokiyo page on the De Vaux / Du Chastel or Marces intercepts found.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry paper or GL.htm entry found; the repo's ledgers (known.py 'Du Chastel', 'Marces') hold only leads.
prior_art.edition: Routledge calendar and CSP Dom. 1658-9 only; Camden Society notes to Nicholas papers cite the Hyde key in BL Egerton MS 2550 p. 85 (web search) but print nothing of this exchange.
prior_art.literature: Three web searches (De Vaux Du Chastel Marces cipher key; Slingsby La Haye July 1659 CSP Dom.; royalist cipher Hyde Nicholas Marces Camden): no study or decipherment of these letters.

vetting.key_check: Not applied (no scan). The partial name key Marces appended (Clarendon vol. 61 f. 426, calendar entry Apr 23/May 3) and 'Cypher Collections vol. VI no. 35g' (De Vaux/Du Chastel, key built from interlined decipherments) are the keys to obtain; none is held in the repo. Hyde's key Egerton 2550 is for a different correspondence.
vetting.duplicates: known.py 'Du Chastel', 'Slingsby', 'Marces': leads 970 (De Vieux, same letter) and 972 (Jul 1659, same letter) closed as duplicates of this lead on 29 Oct 2026; lead 975 (Heath/Mordaunt) is separate. Keep 906.

entries.title: The French ambassador in England (Chateauneuf) to Courcelles in Scotland, two letters in cipher with no decipher listed (entries 72 and 73)

entries.why: French embassy cipher of 1586 at the moment of the Babington plot and Mary's trial; Courcelles was the French link to James VI.

prior_art.decode: Not on DECODE: known.py (Lope de Soria, Soria, plus the correspondent) searched the DECODE view dumps, Cryptoole snapshot and ledgers; the only DECODE Soria records are R9488-R9498 (Soria's outgoing 1523 letters, RAH Salazar A-28) and R9487; none is a letter to Soria. A web search for DECODE + Lope de Soria + cipher found no record of this archive.
prior_art.tomokiyo: Tomokiyo's 'Spanish ciphers during the reign of Charles V' page (copy in this repo, targets/vasto1527/prior/spanish2C_now.htm) read 29 Oct 2026: it lists Ko.6 (Soria, to the Emperor, 1523-27), Soria's Cipher 2 (Galende Diaz) and Luo's Lu.32 (Soria / Charles V / Comendador Mayor, 1532-39); no letter of this archive is read or cited. Web search (Tomokiyo + Lope de Soria + Venice/Genoa) found nothing further.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry or HistoCrypt item on Lope de Soria's incoming correspondence found: searched DECODE + Lope de Soria + Ferdinand/Charles V 1535 and Lasry/Tomokiyo + Charles V + Soria; the Lasry-solved Charles V material found concerns 1547 Saint-Mauris and Renard, not this archive.
prior_art.edition: The 1931 catalogue itself says the cipher part is not translated ('sin traducir'). Rodriguez Villa, Italia desde la batalla de Pavia (1525-27) and Memorias para el saco de Roma print Soria letters of other years; Calendar of State Papers Spain (British History Online) calendars Soria's own despatches (e.g. 1528, 1535, May 1537), not this incoming letter. No edition of this letter found.
prior_art.literature: Galende Diaz, 'La correspondencia cifrada del embajador Lope de Soria', Hispania LII/181 (1992) pp. 493-520, is the study of his ciphers (listed in the RAH DBE entry and by Tomokiyo); not read here (no access), so whether it reproduces any of these letters is unknown. RAH DBE records the archive as RAH Coleccion Lope de Soria 9/1951-1954 and 9/7517-7520 with copies in Salazar, BNE ms. 917, Simancas and BL Add MS 28590 ff. (Soria-Charles V copies 1525-38); present location of the 1931 offered originals is therefore plausibly RAH, but not confirmed.

vetting.key_check: Held here: Soria's own keys A and B (targets/soria1523, soria1527; 1523-27, Soria to the Emperor), which are the wrong direction and years for an incoming letter, and not applied (no images). Named but not held (print only): Luo's Lu.32, used by Lope de Soria and Charles V in 1532-39 (Tomokiyo's page), and Galende Diaz's Soria cipher 2 (1992 appendix); Lu.32 is the first candidate once images are had. Not tested: no scan exists to test against.
vetting.duplicates: known.py run on 'Lope de Soria' and 'Charles V': hits are only sibling leads of the same 1931 catalogue (other item numbers) and the outgoing-direction targets soria1523/soria1527 (Soria to Charles V), none the same letter; catalogue.json has no Soria incoming letter. Item 103 only; item 99 is lead 1099.

prior_art.lasry: No Lasry or HistoCrypt item on Lope de Soria's incoming correspondence found: searched DECODE + Lope de Soria + Ferdinand/Charles V 1535 and Lasry/Tomokiyo + Charles V + Soria; the Lasry-solved Charles V material found concerns 1547 Saint-Mauris and Renard, not this archive.
prior_art.edition: The 1931 catalogue itself says the cipher part is not translated ('sin traducir'). Rodriguez Villa, Italia desde la batalla de Pavia (1525-27) and Memorias para el saco de Roma print Soria letters of other years; Calendar of State Papers Spain (British History Online) calendars Soria's own despatches (e.g. 1528, 1535, May 1537), not this incoming letter. No edition of this letter found.
prior_art.literature: Galende Diaz, 'La correspondencia cifrada del embajador Lope de Soria', Hispania LII/181 (1992) pp. 493-520, is the study of his ciphers (listed in the RAH DBE entry and by Tomokiyo); not read here (no access), so whether it reproduces any of these letters is unknown. RAH DBE records the archive as RAH Coleccion Lope de Soria 9/1951-1954 and 9/7517-7520 with copies in Salazar, BNE ms. 917, Simancas and BL Add MS 28590 ff. (Soria-Charles V copies 1525-38); present location of the 1931 offered originals is therefore plausibly RAH, but not confirmed.

vetting.key_check: Held here: Soria's keys A/B, not applied (wrong correspondent). Named but not held (print only): Luo's Lu.15 (Cifuentes 1533-36). The margin translations would let Lu.15 be verified in one passage. Not tested: no scan.
vetting.duplicates: known.py run on 'Lope de Soria' and 'Cifuentes': hits are only sibling leads of the same 1931 catalogue (other item numbers) and the outgoing-direction targets soria1523/soria1527 (Soria to Charles V), none the same letter; catalogue.json has no Soria incoming letter. Item 214 only; item 213 (31 Jan 1536, Cifuentes to Soria) is not marked cipher.

entries.status: Catalogue: 'Lettre chiffrée sur les affaires de Pologne'. Eight neighbouring sheets are 'Mise en clair d'une dépêche chiffrée' (nos. 237-239, 242, 244, 245, 249, 253), i.e. clear versions of Hacki's own cipher letters, plus the glossed no. 228: the key can be rebuilt from them. No decipherment of the ciphered sheets themselves is noted. Not on DECODE (known.py, 28 Oct 2026). Checked 28 Oct 2026: 28 Oct 2026 verify: Calames confirms no. 234 (16 Nov 1668) as 'Lettre chiffrée sur les affaires de Pologne'; no images online, no published decipherment found. Neighbouring clear 'mise en clair' sheets remain the route to a key. Printed-edition check, 28 Oct 2026: Partly in print. Arckenholtz, Mémoires concernant Christine reine de Suède, t. III (Amsterdam 1759), section on the Polish election (pp. ~340-390): extracts and paraphrases of Père Prieur Hacki's despatches and Christina's instruction to him, from 'Negoziati di Polonia'; the dated Hacki letters (31 Oct 1668-19 Apr 1669) are not printed in full Arckenholtz notes that he holds Christina's ciphers (four kinds, from Rome) and that some of her ciphered letters are undeciphered in print. His source is a Roman/Neapolitan collection, not shown to be Montpellier H 258. Extracts give context and some cribs (nuncio, Neubourg, Moscovite) but not the letters.
entries.why: Christina's own campaign for the Polish crown in 1668-69 (Jean Casimir's abdication), told by her agent in cipher.

VII (its Talon letters come from Pays-Bas and Mélanges Colbert minutes; Ms 1485 is a Turenne recueil and is not cited). Keep open; the clear Pays-Bas minutes are a possible crib source.

entries.status: Cipher found and broken (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026, targets/dormer1694): one simple substitution, numbers 1-25 with dots, in letters signed 'Ex Conde' and pseudonyms (Rojo, Zabulón, El Chismoso; writers not identified), Barcelona, Mataró, Hostalric, Zaragoza 1693-1696, views 132-197 of the BNE digitisation, including an inserted slip wholly in cipher (fol. 190r-v). Key partial by the contributor's protocol (held-out measurements 0.577 and 0.594 against a 0.60 threshold). Slip recto and later passages read, slip verso read in part (line ends in the binding). View 10 holds one line in another system, not treated. Earlier note: BNE catalogue: some letters ciphered. No decipherment noted. Not on DECODE.

seen.extent: Second half, openings 1-2 = ff. 129r-130r: one letter from a correspondent signing 'El Conde ... Rojo' (reading uncertain) to 'Sr. Diego Josef Dormer', dateline 'Marzo 6 de 169?' (last digit uncertain). On f.129r about 6 lines of clear text are followed by runs of dotted numbers (e.g. '8.15.14.8.19.21.11.15' and a run of about 14 numbers) and more such runs on f.129v. In all about 5-8 runs of 8-14 numbers inside the clear lines; clear text on f.130r. Every sampled opening of the first half (about 30 openings) showed plain cursive letters at viewer size, but cipher in them could be missed at the sampling scale. Where the other ciphered letters named in the BNE summary ('varias cartas firmadas por El Milanes y otros seudonimos, algunas cifradas') are was not found.
seen.cipher: Numbers separated by full stops used for single words or names inside a clear letter (a numeral nomenclator or syllabary); no interlinear plaintext, marginal gloss or key table on ff. 129-130. Nothing else in the volume was seen with a decipherment. BNE card: 259 h., 'La mayoria de las h. solo escrito el recto'.

entries.known: Leaves identified (4 Nov 2026, targets/tranchedini1446/): the cipher is on f.134 (27 Nov, short runs of signs with contemporary interlinear glosses: gente d'arme in Toscana, alle stantie, fiorentini, and 'non' over the double-comb sign) and f.139 (29 Nov, Alamanni and Nicodemo, one page of long runs among clear words). f.135 and f.147 are clear letters; R7909 is the Duke's f.145. f.139 transcribed once (778 signs, 31% unmatched shapes, labels over-split): the Domnina 1454 / Lasry 1452 table reads 'cento mila' on line 3 and the comb = non, and the bar-o-bar-o sign (Veneziani in the 1454 tables, but glossed 'del duca' on f.134) closes runs after 'la via' (tentative: la via del duca), and over 54 stretches the table values score z 3.9 against shuffled values (no-space Italian model; an earlier z 2.5 used the wrong model), with readable fragments such as 'qui hauete che', 'cento mila', 'milia', 'et sforza'; the 31% unmatched shapes (nomenclator, syllables) are not read, and solvers fail their held-out controls. No decipherment of either folio found.
entries.open: f.139 not read: an automatic sign inventory now exists (73 types); needs the unmatched shapes read from clear context, the 1446 nomenclator (word signs for stantie, Fiorentini ...) from the f.134 glosses, then a crib attack on the runs between clear words; f.134 glosses not aligned sign by sign. f.133, f.132, f.126, f.162 (other Nicodemo letters of 25-30 Nov per Mazzatinti) are not on these DECODE records.

Many leaves carry interlinear or filed contemporary decipherments that Mazzatinti does not always note (seen: 1584 f. 15 followed by an unlisted clear f. 16 of the same date; a cipher block on canvas 235 has interlinear glosses), so 'read at the time' must be ruled out leaf by leaf. entries.vetting_note: Cipher seen 3 Nov 2026 on Gallica italien 1591 (btv1b100373919, image index 358-359 = f.348-349): Bianco's letter from Lyon 6 June 1466, clear text then about 14 lines of cipher on f.348 and about 9 more on f.349 before the signature, no gloss. Unvetted because the covering editions cannot be opened: Mandrot, Depeches des ambassadeurs milanais IV (1923; not on archive.org) and Kendall-Ilardi, Dispatches vol. III (1981, borrow-only, 401 on full text). A printed decipherment cannot be excluded.

seen.where: Gallica BnF italien 1591 (https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b100373919), images 358 and 359 fetched at 1400 px from https://openapi.bnf.fr/iiif/image/v3/ark:/12148/btv1b100373919/f358/full/1400,/0/default.jpg and f359, plus f357, f360 and f361 at 700-1400 px, viewed 4 Nov 2026. Microfilm (black and white) copy.
seen.extent: Image 358 right page = f.348 (top-right '348', head '1466, 6 jun'): about 16 lines of clear Italian news, then about 13 lines of cipher at the foot. Image 359 left page (continuation of the same sheet): 3 lines of clear text, about 9 lines of cipher, then 3 clear lines, the dateline 'Ex Lugduno die vj Junii 1466' and the signature 'Johannes Blanchus' (reading of the second word uncertain), with the address 'Illmo principi ... domino Galeaz Maria Sforcia vicecomiti duci Mediolani' on the folded verso. About 22 lines of cipher in all.
seen.cipher: Continuous strings of a few stroked shapes (m, n, c, e, a-like forms with bars, dots and a crossed variant), no word division, set in the middle of the clear letter. No interlinear or marginal plaintext on either leaf; neighbouring leaves are other letters (f.347 a copy of a Venetian letter of 6 June, f.349 a clear letter of Firmo de Landriano of 11 June, f.360 another letter), so no separate decipherment is filed beside it.

entries.title: Ferdinand I → Giovanni Battista Castaldo (Transylvania), four Latin letters with long cipher passages
entries.correspondents: Ferdinand I, King of the Romans → Giovanni Battista Castaldo, imperial commander in Hungary/Transylvania
entries.shelfmark: Milan, Biblioteca Ambrosiana, G 275 inf., unità codicologiche 3, 9, 10, 11 (ff. 9r-15v, 34r-36v, 37r-42v, 43r-48v)
entries.folio_note: About 25 leaves; c. 10r is a full page of symbol cipher (c. 25 lines, cipher signs: digits, letters, Greek-like and arbitrary signs) with a contemporary Latin decipherment of part of it in the left margin; c. 35r is a full page of cipher with no decipherment. entries.status: OPAC: "Lettera a Giovanni Battista Castaldo con testo cifrato" (four records). Not on DECODE; no repo hit (known.py: Castaldo, G 275).

entries.folio_note: "3 lettere originali completamente in cifra a lui dirette" (20 Oct, 23 Oct 1618 and one more), with loose sheets of Spinelli's residence archive; extent of cipher not given
entries.status: Tiepolo's 1965 inventory (transcribed 2020) lists them as wholly in cipher; no decipherment noted, unlike the Costantinopoli items of the same inventory where 'decifrazione' is stated. entries.why: October 1618 is the height of Venice's quarrel with the viceroy Osuna and the aftermath of the 'Spanish conspiracy'; instructions sent to the Naples resident in full cipher were the most secret part of that correspondence.

entries.title: Trémais → the minister, cipher letter, Montréal
entries.correspondents: Charles-François Pichot de Querdisien Trémais (commissaire sent to audit Bigot) → minister of the Marine
entries.shelfmark: ANOM, COL C11A 104, ff.346-347v (CABAC_PIAF_60950)
entries.folio_note: 3 images
entries.status: Still open (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026), two facts for the entry. (a) The PREVIOUS Trémais cipher letter, 22 Sept 1759, is at ff. 342-343v (New France Archives NFA 27540) and is existing: its contemporary decipherment is bound right after it, ff. 344-345 ('Copie de la lettre en chiffre de M. Querdisien Trémais, dattée du Canada le 22 7bre 1759'), and is copied in the LAC C11A transcripts, reel C-2402 (vol. 104 part 2) pp. 523-527, with a bureau note dated 21 Nov 1759 ('cela ne dit rien et n'éclaircit rien...'). (b) The 6 Nov letter is the covering letter for a copy of the 22 Sept one, mostly in clear with cipher runs; it is NOT in the transcript. Trémais's code is his own, not the Vaudreuil C11E 10 table (0.063 against a best of 0.229 for 200 shuffled keys on f. 342). A partial key rebuilt from the 22 Sept pair by known plaintext reaches 0.704 on a held-out page (best shuffled 0.272): real but incomplete, not validated. Images are only 624-1125 px; HD scans are needed. Earlier note: Title only ("Lettre chiffrée ... au ministre"), no content summary, unlike the deciphered despatches around it: the ANOM/LAC describers apparently could not read it. Not on DECODE, not in repo. Trémais was sent in 1758 to investigate the Bigot frauds; his cipher may differ from Vaudreuil's.
entries.why: Secret report of the investigator behind the "Affaire du Canada" (Bigot trial), just after the fall of Quebec.
