seen.where: NAA: MP1049/1, 1916/0235, item 400554, 338 pages, read in Chrome via SearchNRetrieve/NAAMedia/ShowImage.aspx?B=400554&S=<page>. Pages viewed: 3, 20, 50, 52, 53, 54, 56, 58, 60, 62 (zoomed), 66, 70, 75, 90, 110, 140, 170, 200, 230, 290, 335; about 21 of 338, a sample, not a full read.
seen.extent: Handwritten station logs of 25 Jul - 4 Aug 1914 start at p. 56. Pages 56, 58, 60, 62, 66 and 70 carry several messages each of 10-letter code words, 5 to 40 words a message, e.g. p. 60 ASB (Scharnhorst) to KCA (Yap), 3 Aug: 'Asintjoung jopsimonado ...'. Total word count not measured. Wheatley's report (pp. 50-53) says copies of all messages of 25 Jul - 4 Aug are attached.
seen.cipher: Artificial 10-letter code words copied by Australian operators from German wireless, with plain German (some with English) in between. Wheatley, 19 Apr 1916, p. 53: 'These were all in the same code, which is evidently a code for the use of men-of-war and important land stations only. It differs very considerably from the Handels Verkehr Buch'. The code-word messages on pp. 56, 58, 60, 66 and 70 have no decipherment written with them. Two decodes are on the leaves: p. 62, one 7-word message glossed in German and English ('From Cruiser squadron. You are to go to Caroline Isles'), and p. 75, 4-letter groups (VGHA OHAG PDLW ...) glossed. So this lead covers the unglossed code-word messages only. Pages 170 and later seen are plain-language translations and minutes.

prior_art.literature: navyhistory.au on Wheatley quotes his 1934 paper: most intercepts were 'in an unknown code' and filed; he later decoded 10-letter HVB groups (two 5-letter parts) under a changed key, on Melbourne Cup Day 1914. That is HVB squadron traffic, and his 1916 report separates this men-of-war code from HVB. NOT opened: Phelps, Australian Code Breakers (2020), and Wheatley's account AWM252 A228, either of which might say more; Room 40 files not searched.

entries.title: Machain (1878), Decoud (1883) and Perousha (1884) → Juan Silvano Godoi, three Paraguayan letters in code
entries.correspondents: Raymundo Machain (Montevideo), Héctor Francisco Decoud, Sofia Perousha → Juan Silvano Godoi
entries.place: Montevideo / Buenos Aires / Asunción exile network
entries.shelfmark: UC Riverside, Special Collections, Juan Silvano Godoi papers (MS 003), letters of 1878-08-08 (mostly in code), 1883-11-02 (partly), 1884-04-23 (partly); Calisphere items
entries.folio_note: Machain 2 leaves mostly code; Decoud and Perousha partial passages
entries.status: Split (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026). (a) Decoud 2 Nov 1883 and Perousha 23 Apr 1884: existing. The Decoud PDF on Calisphere (curivsc_003_004_055, image 7) holds a typed sheet 'Key to Code in Hector Francisco Decoud's Letters - Decoded by Harris G. Warren May 29, 1980' (A6 B7 C8 D9 E1 F2 G3 H4 I5 J10 L11 M13 N14 O16 P17 Q18 R19 S20 T21 U22 V23 X24 Y25 Z26). It reads all of Decoud's number runs (revolucion, Adolfo, Jara, frustrado [sic], planes, paraguayos, Marcelina, Antonio Taboada) and Perousha's (siempre, permitiras, siempre); the pencil note on Perousha reads '(Clave revolucionaria)'. (b) Machain 8 Aug 1878 (curivsc_003_005_046): a different system, single Latin letters plus ll, rr, ñ, about 330 symbols in 11 runs. Still open: simple substitution, Caesar/affine over 26-29-letter Spanish alphabets, periodic Vigenère and per-word Vigenère all fail; IC 0.052; long exact repeats (9 symbols at distance 73, 7 at 57) point to a homophonic or nomenclator-like letter system. Earlier note: Item-level finding-aid text: 'mostly written in code', 'writes partially in code on the possibility of revolutionary undertaking', 'partly in code'. No key or decipherment noted. Not on DECODE. known.py: no hits for Godoi.
entries.why: Exile conspiracy letters of Paraguayan politicians after the War of the Triple Alliance; a rare Latin American 19th-century nomenclator with a known plaintext language.
entries.score_note: Scored from the hub's catalogue description during the Oct 2026 DPLA/Smithsonian sweep (research/dpla_smithsonian/); not viewed
entries.verify: View the three Calisphere items; check the other Godoi correspondence in the same folders for sibling letters with glosses or a key.

entries.title: Carta cifrada on a joint Mexican-Colombian expedition to free Cuba from Spain
entries.correspondents: unknown
entries.shelfmark: AGN México, Gobernación, vol. 85, exp. 2
entries.folio_note: One expediente, sección s/s, "Correspondencia"
entries.status: AGN Guía: "Carta cifrada donde se habla de una expedición a Cuba, para liberarla del dominio español, utilizando fuerzas armadas tanto de la República Mexicana como de Colombia." The content is known to the cataloguer, so a decipherment or clear copy may accompany it.

entries.title: Magonista letters intercepted at St. Louis: consul's transcriptions, some in cipher "no se encuentran descifradas", with a sibling file of deciphered letters and key lists
entries.correspondents: Ricardo Flores Magón and Partido Liberal Mexicano members ↔ correspondents in Mexico and the US (intercepted; transcribed by the Mexican consul at St. Louis → Secretaría de Gobernación)
entries.shelfmark: AGN México, Gobernación, vol. 802 exp. 2; vol. 803 exp. 2 and exp. 4 (cipher letters not deciphered); vol. 803 exp. 3 (letters "con clave descifrada" and "relaciones de claves que utilizaban")
entries.folio_note: Transcriptions; number of cipher letters unknown
entries.status: AGN Guía: vol. 802 exp. 2 and vol. 803 exp. 2: "algunas cartas vienen en clave y no se encuentran descifradas"; vol. 803 exp. 4: "algunas cartas cifradas"; vol. 803 exp. 3: some letters deciphered and lists of the keys they used. Narváez 2015 shows the 1907-08 magonista systems were simple substitutions on names (from AHDSREM 11-4-198 and L-E-954), not these AGN files.
entries.why: Organisation of the 1908 PLM uprising; the cipher passages hide the names of the clubs' contacts inside Mexico, which the Díaz government was hunting.

entries.title: Secretaría de Gobernación political-police cipher telegrams (DGIPS), elections, Cristero-era arrests of priests, sedition

entries.folio_note: About 1,100 expedientes (80 matched "cifrado", 1,030 "cifrados"; all but one of the latter are DGIPS files), each with one or a few telegrams described "Telegrama(s) cifrado(s)"

entries.why: Internal security reporting on the Cristero conflict, the 1929 and 1940 elections and right-wing conspiracies; low per item.

entries.title: Porfirio Díaz (and his secretary Rafael Chousal) → Gen. Bernardo Reyes: about 45 cipher telegrams the catalogue marks "sin traducción"
entries.correspondents: President Porfirio Díaz; Rafael Chousal; Ignacio M. Escudero; Felipe Berriozábal; Blas Escontría; J. Y. Limantour → Gen. Bernardo Reyes (Monterrey)
entries.place: Mexico City (one from Cuernavaca, one from San Luis Potosí)
entries.folio_note: One telegram each; the catalogue lists 52 untranslated cipher records in fondo DLI (list in cehm_sintraduccion.json), about 2,100 records typed "telegrama cifrado" in all, most with summaries
entries.status: CEHM records read "Sin traducción" / "[Legajo sin traducción]" with type "Telegrama cifrado"; hundreds of sibling Díaz-Reyes cipher telegrams in the same fondo carry summaries of their content, so a key can be rebuilt from translated pairs. Ángel & Morales-Luna 2008 print a Díaz substitution table (Díaz-Bravo) from the Porfirio Díaz archive (Universidad Iberoamericana).
entries.why: Díaz's direct orders to his northern proconsul across 25 years (Coahuila 1885-86, the Garza revolt 1891-92, the Reyes crisis of July 1909); the untranslated ones are exactly those whose content is unknown.
entries.score_note: Scored from the CEHM online catalogue record during the Oct 2026 Mexico sweep (research/latam_mexico/); not viewed
entries.verify: View a translated and an untranslated telegram of the same month at CEHM (e.g. DLI.5.907.1 against its Oct 1886 neighbours); check whether the Díaz telegrams use the same table as the Díaz archive at UIA; Narváez 2019 ch. VI.

entries.title: Maderista junta at El Paso: telegrams "texto en clave" that the catalogue leaves undeciphered, among hundreds deciphered at the time
entries.correspondents: Gustavo A. Madero, Francisco Vázquez Gómez, agents at Ojinaga, San Antonio, Douglas → Federico González Garza (alias W. Olliphant, Fred García), Adolfo González (alias John McCarty), Braulio Hernández; 1914: telegrams to Francisco Villa and Gov. Fidel Ávila
entries.place: El Paso, San Antonio, Washington, Ojinaga
entries.folio_note: CMXV.14.1354.1 viewed (one 45-number telegram); 24 other undeciphered records unviewed.
entries.status: CEHM: "TEXTO EN CLAVE" with no decipherment, against dozens of sibling records "TEXTO EN CLAVE Y DESCIFRADO" in the same legajos; CMXV.18.1795.1 is a typed transcription of the decipherments of 66 coded telegrams (Jan-May 1911) and CMXV.16.1557.1 holds 21 manuscript keys ("clave Madero, letras más frecuentes", "clave G.A.", "clave de los reyistas", División del Norte alfabeto).
entries.why: Command traffic of the Madero revolution in its decisive weeks (Ojinaga, Agua Prieta, the armistice and the taking of Ciudad Juárez, May 1911); 1914 items are Villa-era Chihuahua.
entries.score_note: Scored from the CEHM online catalogue record during the Oct 2026 Mexico sweep (research/latam_mexico/); not viewed

entries.title: Military report wholly "en clave" from Puente Nacional during Santa Anna's 1832 rising

entries.title: Federal (Huertista) army telegrams "en clave" in Gen. Guillermo Rubio Navarrete's papers: Lampazos, Monterrey, Laredo, Zacatecas
entries.correspondents: Federal commanders in Nuevo León and Zacatecas (José Domínguez Guevara, Joaquín Téllez and others) ↔ Gen. Guillermo Rubio Navarrete
entries.place: Lampazos, Monterrey, Laredo, Zacatecas, Tamarindo, San Francisco
entries.folio_note: About 20 telegrams and letters recorded only as "EN CLAVE" (some incomplete); the same legajos hold the keys: DLXXIII.1.28.8-23 (alphabet and syllables), 1.28.14-23 ("Clave núm. 109, Secretaría de Guerra y Marina", military vocabulary), 1.29.15-30 (alphabets, syllables and numbers, Zacatecas)
entries.status: CEHM: "EN CLAVE", no translation; a few siblings carry summaries (1.29.9-30, 2.41.18-41: railway repaired to Gutiérrez north of Fresnillo). Key sheets of the Secretaría de Guerra filed with them. Narrowed 30 Oct 2026: three telegrams in Clave núm. 109 (1.30.16-49, 2.41.9-41, 2.41.13-41) were read by Brice Dudout (write-up rubio1913); the other pieces use other tables and are unread.
entries.why: Federal army operations against Pablo González and Carranza in the Northeast (Lampazos, Candela, Cañón de Sabinas, Nov 1913) and the defence of Zacatecas before June 1914; Huerta-side cipher is rarely seen.
entries.score_note: Scored from the CEHM online catalogue record during the Oct 2026 Mexico sweep (research/latam_mexico/); not viewed
entries.verify: View the key sheets (1.28.8-23, 1.28.14-23, 1.29.15-30) and one telegram (1.30.17-49) at CEHM.

entries.title: Cipher telegrams to Setembrino de Carvalho, federal commander in Ceará (Juazeiro sedition)
entries.correspondents: Rio de Janeiro (Pamplona and others) → Fernando Setembrino de Carvalho
entries.shelfmark: CPDOC/FGV, Arquivo Fernando Setembrino de Carvalho, FSC pce 1914.03.10/4
entries.folio_note: 16 images (DocReader bib FSC_PACEARA pagfis 1317-1332): 12 telegrams 10 Mar - 20 May 1914, 10 with cipher (~200 words, most repeated as service check), from Pamplona, Vespasiano de Albuquerque and Rego Barros. Pencil decipherment of the whole cipher text on the 14 Mar telegram (pagfis 1319); pencil attempt on two words of pagfis 1326. Transcription sample: research/latam_vetting/1470_sample.txt.
entries.status: CPDOC summary 'Telegramas cifrados a Setembrino de Carvalho'. Image of the first telegram viewed 28 Oct 2026: letter cipher, no decipherment on the sheet. Cribs in the same digitised fonds: FSC cont 1914.10.07/2 (two War Ministry cipher words glossed) and FSC pce 1914.02.19/2 (typed clear copies of Vespasiano's telegrams to Setembrino, one acknowledging 'mais dois cifrados'). Not on DECODE, not in the repo. Vetted 28 Oct 2026: Vigenère, 8-letter key restarted per word; key MFTDBSJV rebuilt from the pencil decipherment on pagfis 1319 reads the Mar-Apr telegrams; 10 Mar (LETCARIV, garbled) and 20 May (about 10-letter key) broke ciphertext-only in minutes. Verdict key_lookup: a small, quick reading, worth doing as a target (key recovered from adjacent plaintext / ciphertext-only), not a catalogue entry.
entries.why: Government cipher traffic during the 1914 federal intervention against the Juazeiro (Padre Cícero) rising in Ceará; Brazilian army/government cipher of 1914 otherwise unknown.
entries.score_note: Scored from the CPDOC description and one image during the Oct 2026 Brazil sweep (research/latam_brazil/)
entries.verify: Page through the 16 images in DocReader; transcribe the groups; test periodic polyalphabetic (Vigenère/Beaufort, Portuguese) and code hypotheses; look for decipherments in neighbouring FSC pce 1914 folders.
entries.prior_art: no prior reading found except the contemporary pencil decipherment of the 14 Mar telegram (checked 28 Oct 2026: DECODE dumps, known.py, web search)
entries.access_note: digitised on CPDOC DocReader (free)

seen.extent: 16 images, 12 telegrams 10 Mar - 20 May 1914, 10 with cipher, about 200 cipher words, most sent twice as body and service repeat.
seen.cipher: Pasted telegraph strips of five-to-ten letter groups, e.g. 10 Mar 'OSNVOJ QEUQ NLXHE OMLVRTCJ OIN BEKVE' with the clear tail 'RESPONDA AMANHA ... = E PAMPLONA'. No decipherment on that sheet. The 14 Mar sheet (pagfis 1319, 'BJLVPS CZX YJ BFKHDW', signed Vespasiano de Albuquerque) carries a pencil decipherment of that one telegram only; the 28 Oct pass recorded a two-word pencil attempt on pagfis 1326. The other telegrams carry none.

entries.title: Benito Varela, Paraguayan foreign minister → Manuel Moreira de Castro, consul general in Rio: letter with numeric cipher passages
entries.correspondents: Benito Varela (Ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Paraguay, under Carlos Antonio López) → Manuel Moreira de Castro (consul general, later plenipotentiary of Paraguay at the court of Brazil)
entries.shelfmark: Asunción, Archivo Nacional de Asunción, Colección Rio Branco, ANA-AHRP-PY-558-1-31 (ex Biblioteca Nacional do Rio de Janeiro I-29,25,23), item 13
entries.folio_note: PDF of 98 images; item 13 on images 41-42 (0-based), sheets 586-587: 12 runs of dot-separated numbers (~90 tokens, values mostly odd 1-49, also 98 and 116), name numbers 25, 1, 116 and a barred-circle sign, in a clear Spanish letter. Transcription: research/latam_vetting/1500_sample.txt.
entries.status: ANA description, item 13: 'se refiere a otros asuntos que no pueden ser identificados por estar escritos en código cifrado' (i.e. the cataloguer could not read it). Viewed on the scan 28 Oct 2026: numeric substitution (letters or syllables) inside a clear letter about Brazil, Rio Grande and Buenos Aires. Not on DECODE, not in the repo. Vetted 28 Oct 2026: scan transcribed; no decipherment on or with it; no key known; not on DECODE, no edition or study found. Verdict open. Next: page through the other 96 images of 558-1-31 and the sibling López-era files for a key or a deciphered copy.
entries.why: Cipher of Carlos Antonio López's foreign ministry with its agent in Rio on the eve of the 1850 Paraguay-Brazil alliance against Rosas; Paraguayan state ciphers of this period are hardly known.
entries.score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 South Cone/Andes sweep (research/latam_southcone/); the cipher page was viewed on the scan.
entries.verify: Transcribe images 41-42 of the PDF; small numbers mostly odd suggest a letter table with homophones or a syllabary; context (Rosas, Brazil, Rio Grande, Urquiza) gives cribs. Look for further Varela/Moreira letters in the Rio Branco collection (ANA-AHRP 558-*) using the same numbers.
entries.prior_art: open (checked 28 Oct 2026: DECODE dumps, known.py, web search for edition and literature; nothing found)
entries.access_note: PDF of the whole file online at the Archivo Nacional de Asunción (cipher on images 41-42)

Printed Paraguayan diplomatic collections were not checked page by page.
prior_art.literature: Web searches in Spanish and English on Carlos Antonio López's diplomatic ciphers (cifra diplomática Paraguay, clave cifrada siglo XIX, criptografía) found no study of a Paraguayan state cipher of this period.

vetting.key_check: No Paraguayan key of the López era is held in the repo or known in print. The sibling diplomatic files of the Rio Branco collection skimmed in the South Cone sweep (Gelly in Rio 1849-52, Decoud 1853, F. S. López 1853, Varela - Derqui 1852) showed no number runs at thumbnail size, and the other 96 images of this file were not paged through for a key in this session. Quick checks here: the repeated runs (9.27.7.33.15.3 twice; 9.13.1.37.3.1?.7.9.33 twice before '[Rio?] Grande') do not fit a plain one-value-per-letter alphabet with an obvious crib ('provincia' would need two values for i and one value for both r and n), so no simple key tried reads it. Not a key lookup on present evidence.

entries.status: AGN description: López Méndez reports the sailing of the schooner Gambier (Capt. Peter Paxtor) with men, arms and powder, that the East India Company ships were not bought and the loan not raised, and 'otras informaciones se hallan consignadas bajo el código de una clave secreta'. No decipherment mentioned. Not on DECODE; known.py: López Méndez no hits. Vetted 28 Oct 2026 on the scans: the cipher is a letter table with superscript row digits (1-7), 15 words in a clear letter. Not printed in the O'Leary volumes on archive.org. Most of it was recovered from context during vetting: López Méndez was jailed five months and freed on bail; MacGregor 'ha causado un perjuicio indecible a nuestra causa'; MacGregor plans to go to Santafé (sample file research/latam_vetting/1523_sample.txt).
entries.why: The independence agents' cipher between London and Angostura in the year of Boyacá; a key here would be the earliest Gran Colombian diplomatic cipher, and a possible ancestor of Revenga's 1822 London-Madrid key (targets/revenga1822).
entries.verify: Open the 24 images in DataViva (detail page) and locate the cipher lines; then check O'Leary, Memorias (Correspondencia / Documentos) and the Archivo del Libertador for a printed or interlined decipherment.

seen.where: AGN Colombia DataViva, record 66b0cd4f151c9d47762a2382 (https://dataviva.archivogeneral.gov.co/explore/agn/detail/66b0cd4f151c9d47762a2382); all 24 images were downloaded through the public API (POST /api/records/public/<unit>/pages with the file's record_id) and viewed. The cipher is on gallery index 11 (f. 227v) and index 12 (f. 228r), in López Méndez's letter of 29 Jan 1819 (ff. 226-228).
seen.extent: Fifteen underlined cipher words, about 70 letters, inside a Spanish clear-text letter: ten words on f. 227v lines 20-22, two words on f. 227v line 27, two words split across f. 227v (last line) and f. 228r (line 1), and one word on f. 228r lines 5-6. Everything else in the unit is in clear (ff. 222-224 Hurry, Powles & Hurry; ff. 230-231 Herring and Saffray; ff. 232-233 a printed loan certificate; ff. 225 and 229 blank).
seen.cipher: A letter substitution in ordinary lowercase letters in which many letters carry a small superscript digit 1-7; the same letter with different digits stands for different plaintext letters (e1=b, e2=f, e3=l, e4=r, e5=t, e7=y), so it is a table cipher of letter plus row number, not a plain monoalphabet. No decipherment is written over or beside the cipher words and the unit holds no key and no clear copy.

prior_art.decode: Not on DECODE: known.py found no hit for López Méndez, Lopez Mendez, MacGregor, Gambier or the shelfmark SAA-I.17 in the DECODE view dumps; only this lead itself.
prior_art.tomokiyo: Not in Tomokiyo's cryptiana: the index page crypto.htm (fetched 28 Oct 2026) has no Bolívar, Gran Colombia or 1819 London page; its only Spanish-American items are a Jesuit cipher from Peru (1601) and a line-segment memorial from Peru (1604).
prior_art.lasry: Nothing by Lasry on this cipher: the GL.htm copies in the repository (targets/gramont1529, targets/vasto1527/prior, targets/esp318/lit/crypt) have no Bolívar, López Méndez or Colombia entry, and his published work is on Spanish and other European ciphers of the 16th-18th centuries.
prior_art.edition: Not found printed. Fifteen volumes of O'Leary's Memorias on archive.org (tomos I, II, VI, IX, XVI, XXII, XXIV, XXV, XXVI, XXVIII pt 2, XXIX, XXX, XXXI and the narrative) were grepped for Paxtor/Paxton, Gambier, 'perjuicio indecible', 'salido con fianza', 'cinco meses' and López Méndez: the only López Méndez letter is a Lima letter of 1826 (tomo IX). The O'Leary volumes of correspondence not on archive.org, Lecuna's Cartas del Libertador (Bolívar's own letters, not letters to him) and the Archivo del Libertador online (did not answer earlier in the sweep) were not checked.
prior_art.literature: Web searches in Spanish and English (López Méndez + Bolívar 1819 + cifra/clave/Gambier/Peter Paxtor; the deciphered phrases 'perjuicio indecible', 'preso', 'fianza' with Mac Gregor) found nothing on this cipher; a Cambridge article on Bolívar's British networks (JLAS 2024) cites López Méndez letters of 1817 but not this one. Galende Díaz 2000 (read in full) summarises Bákula 1949: Bolívar's key 'revealed by O'Leary' is a simple substitution whose only difficulty is the word division, unlike this superscript table. Bákula 1949 itself was not reachable.

vetting.key_check: No held key reads it. The Revenga 1822 key (targets/revenga1822) is a monoalphabetic substitution with a = word space and no superscripts, and Crawford 1813 is the JQA numeric code, so neither fits. Bolívar's key as Galende 2000 n. 41 describes it after Bákula (simple substitution) and Santander's (two interleaved half-alphabets, n. 45) are single alphabets and cannot give one letter several values by superscript. Without a key, most of the passage was recovered here from context and the clear text alone: 'que he estado preso cinco meses y he salido con fianza', 'Mac Gregor', 'para Mar...caibo?' and 'ir á Santafé' (sample in research/latam_vetting/1523_sample.txt). The structure of the table (letter plus row digit) and four values (plain e, m6, r1, plain t) remain open.

No DECODE id, catalogue entry or target folder covers López Méndez to Bolívar, 29 Jan 1819.

entries.title: Brig. Gen. C. C. Augur (Dept of Texas) to Lt Gen Sheridan and Maj. G. B. Russell: three 'Cypher' telegrams during the Texas gubernatorial crisis (Davis/Coke), Jan 1874
entries.correspondents: C. C. Augur to P. H. Sheridan (Chicago); Augur to G. B. Russell (Austin)
entries.place: San Antonio, Texas (HQ Department of Texas)
entries.shelfmark: Newberry Library, Ayer MS 3008 (Christopher C. Augur papers, letter-books of the Departments of Texas and the Gulf), box 02, scan 00045-1; telegram nos. 8529 and following
entries.folio_note: one scan page with three telegrams of about 50-60 words each, copied as scrambled English words (word transposition, with 'Cypher' left as a stray word); more cipher telegrams may sit elsewhere in the 1873-74 letter-books
entries.status: Newberry's volunteer transcription (Newberry Transcribe) types the three telegrams as scrambled word strings, e.g. 'Dresden I persons to it fussy unauthorized forward ... Cypher state Grant ...'; no plaintext is given. The 18 Feb 1869 letter in Ayer MS 3039 (Grierson papers, box 03 f.153) describes the army cypher method then used in Texas: write the message in 4 to 9 columns, a key sets the reading order, key words are substituted. Not checked on DECODE beyond known.py (no hit for Augur cipher). Scan viewed 29 Oct 2026 (collections.newberry.org, Image w/ Text): letter-book page 31 with telegrams 8529 (to Sheridan, 12 Jan 1874), 30 and 45 (to Russell, 12 and 17 Jan 1874) in clerk's hand as scrambled English words with code words (Dresden, Cheyenne, Neces, Houston, Waco); no decipherment on the page.
entries.why: Augur's private cipher traffic with Sheridan during the Jan 1874 Texas political crisis (Governor Davis refusing to yield to Coke) would show what the army told Washington; also a clean test of a US Army word-transposition cipher with a described key.
entries.score_note: Scored during the Oct 2026 Chicago Collections Consortium sweep (research/chi_consortium/); scan viewed 29 Oct 2026 in Newberry Digital Collections
entries.verify: Open the scan (collections.newberry.org asset 2KXJ8ZSFQY9EQ) and check the ciphertext is the scrambled words and not a decipherment printed in cipher order; read the 18 Feb 1869 key letter (Ayer MS 3039 box 03 f.153, asset 2KXJ8ZSC7CU0W) and its second page for the column-order rule; try 4-9 column transpositions with nulls.

seen.extent: c. 9r clear Spanish text; c. 10r about 22 lines of cipher (signs plus syllabic groups such as lab, leb, den, gos, pre, ral) from the fifth line down; c. 11r about 14 lines of cipher in two blocks, then 'De Genoua a vij de março M.D.xxvij' and the signature; cc. 9v, 10v, 11v, 12r/v carry no further cipher
seen.cipher: Spanish letter, signed Genoa 7 March 1527, partly in cipher: a mixed system of single signs (loops, crosses, 4, L, 11, 3) and three-letter syllabic groups (lab, leb, den, gos). The cipher stretches are written in the running text with no interlinear or marginal plaintext, and no separate clear copy or decipherment is filed with the four leaves (cc. 9-12); the blank leaves carry only the address and a later hand 'Lope de Soria'.

entries.status: Note (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026): the BNE records of RES/261/55-61 are not cipher (55 = Elisabeth Charlotte d'Orléans to Charles II, Fontainebleau 16 Sept 1679; the others are autograph royal letters in clear). Of the 98 RES/261 records only /58 (this letter) and /73 (lead 1600) are cipher, and /73 is Diego Hurtado de Mendoza to Granvelle, Rome 1548 (imperial cipher of 1544-54, see lead 1600's vetting), so the series holds no sibling or key for Leopold's cipher. Earlier note: BNE title: 'Carta cifrada del Emperador Leopoldo I a Carlos II de España'; autograph, wax seal. No decipherment noted on the card. Not on DECODE. Viewed 4 Nov 2026 (BNE Digital page 5): numeric cipher, no decipherment on the leaf.

seen.extent: One folio (page 5): a clear opening line ('Ser.mo Rey Carlos(?) ... He recibido la carta de V. Magd. de 8 de febrero y holgado de veer en ella') then about 21 lines of numbers, roughly 11 per line (about 240 groups by eye, not measured; 2- and 3-digit values up to 224, many struck through), ending in a clear closing ('Guarde Dios a V. Magd. como deseo. Praga 14 de Abril 1680. Buen tio y hermano de V. Mag. [signature]'). Page 6 is the verso showing through.
seen.cipher: Numeric cipher (values about 12-224, some groups such as 224 and 62 39 recurring, underlined or struck through in the usual way) set between a clear opening and a clear closing. No interlinear decipherment, no margin gloss, no key sheet and no claro on any of the 10 pages; only library marks (RES/261/58, 18632).

No interlinear decipherment, no key on any of the 10 pages. A letter-level homophonic annealer failed two same-size controls (4-22% letters correct), so its output on the letter was rejected. No key or decipherment found online or in the repo.
entries.open: The whole letter (cipher system not established: letter, syllable or nomenclator). Needs a key: Auer's chapter on imperial ciphers (Kryptologie im fruehneuzeitlichen Europa), the Spain chapter of the same volume, OeStA and AHN Estado holdings, or a deciphered sibling (RES/261/73, catalogue 1600). Otherwise a structural attack on the value blocks.

entries.title: Swedish letters to Axel Oxenstierna, June 1633, code numbers glossed in part (R4338-R4341)
entries.correspondents: unknown → Camerarius?, Amsterdam; Rusdorff → Oxenstierna; Swedish agent → Oxenstierna

entries.status: DECODE R4284–R4341, 8 records in four different ciphers, each its own entry since the one-key split of 14 Oct 2026. Viewed 21 Sept 2026. The two Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330–R4331, riksarkivet1628.html) are read and removed from this entry; R4282 was deciphered by George Lasry (decode4282.html). R4306: contributed partial Dutch decipherment by George Lasry, transcribed with CTTS then solved with Opus 5.5 (17 Oct 2026; sweden4306.html, which also records this project's failed attempt of 21 Sept 2026); pencilled 1632? and Amsterdam attribution remain qualified, four code identities open. R4336–R4337 turned out to be Rusdorff's London letters of February 1625 in a homophonic cipher with an alphabetical nomenclator; key recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry (21 Oct 2026, PR #72; rusdorff1625.html) and removed from this entry. Open: R4284 (Latin 1628, Camerarius docket; riksarkivet4284.html) — attacked with Latin annealing and against two box keys, not broken; R4333–R4335 (Rusdorff → Oxenstierna 1628, another cipher; rusdorff1628.html) and R4338–R4341 (E 708, Swedish, June 1633, not 1646; glossed in part at the time; oxenstierna1633.html) surveyed only. Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
entries.why: One remaining key-box ciphertext that resisted a first attack, and Oxenstierna correspondence of 1628 and 1633 with a key collection that may hold their keys.
entries.score_note: Scored by rule from DECODE metadata (class from key signals, solvability from key, length and language, importance from the correspondents); not yet reviewed by hand.

entries.known: Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330-R4331) deciphered in full here, key recovered from the interlinear glosses (riksarkivet1628). R4282 key recovered ciphertext-only by George Lasry (decode4282, PR #33). R4306 deciphered in part by George Lasry with CTTS and Opus 5.5, 17 Oct 2026 (sweden4306, PR #42); four code values open. R4336-R4337 (Rusdorff, London, Feb 1625) key recovered ciphertext-only by George Lasry with CTTS and Claude Opus 5.5, 21 Oct 2026 (rusdorff1625, PR #72); codes 628 and 701 open.

entries.title: Lovisa Ulrika correspondence, system A: 6 Mar 1764 and the glossed letter of 15 Nov 1765
entries.correspondents: C.W. von Düben / N.P. Gyldenstolpe → Queen Lovisa Ulrika (and each other)
entries.shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Kungliga arkiv, Drottning Lovisa Ulrika, Utgångna skrivelser, SE/RA/710003/02/008/b/K 259, images 101-102, 124-126
entries.folio_note: 223 images online (IIIF A0073297). Image 107: a full page of 3-digit numeric cipher (groups 17-720, dot-separated) facing a French clear page mentioning the Empress, Saldern; several more all-cipher pages around images 60-125 in a sampled contact sheet; images ~216-220 a folder "Chiffernycklar" and three key tables.
entries.status: Catalogue: "Drottning Lovisa Ulrikas hemliga korrespondens. Brev från C.W. von Düben till N.P. Gyldenstolpe och Lovisa Ulrika 1764-1765 ... Chiffernycklar." Not on DECODE (no Lovisa Ulrika record), not in the repo. No decipherment seen on the sampled pages; interlinear decipherment not checked page by page. The 24 Oct Riksarkivet sweep listed K 259 as keys only; the 26 Oct sample (image 107) shows a full page of numeric cipher. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): Frederick II's letter of 3 March 1765 in this group is printed in the Politische Correspondenz, vol. 24, no. 15458 (one letter; Düben's code letters unaffected; targets/duben1764/). Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
entries.why: The queen's private cipher channel during the 1764-66 Hat/Cap crisis and her dealings with Russia and Prussia; the keys sit in the same volume, so it should read quickly.
entries.score_note: Scored from the archive description and a sampled contact sheet of the online scans during the Oct 2026 Riksarkivet sweep (research/scandinavia/)
entries.verify: Page through the 223 images (bildvisning A0073297), list the cipher pages, check for interlinear decipherments, transcribe the key tables at images ~217-220 and test them on image 107.

seen.where: Gelders Archief, 0439 Huizen Waardenburg en Neerijnen, inv. 124, https://permalink.geldersarchief.nl/CA57BD7A9396402C8AFC64E42D37AC0E (viewer read in Chrome); APE record 0439-124 confirms the title.
seen.extent: All 64 scans of the folder viewed in this pass (scans 1-13, 16, 26 at full viewer width, the rest at 0.75 of it; scan 8 also zoomed in the viewer). Duncan's letters in French, docketed 1730 Jan 28 to 1731. Blank or nearly blank versos: 24, 28, 32, 39, 40, 52, 56, 60. Ciphertext on 4 scans, belonging to two letters: scans 1-4 (signed 'L... 20 Janvier 1730', Q: N:) and scans 5-8 (docket '1730 ... 30'). About 17 lines of cipher by eye, not measured: scan 2 two lines, scan 6 about seven, scan 7 about six, scan 8 two. The other 60 scans have no cipher strings, including all the 'Pour vous seul' letters (scans 9, 21, 25, 29, 33, 37, 41, 45, 49, 53, 57, 61).
seen.cipher: Actual ciphertext: unbroken runs of digits mixed with a few letter forms, set inside clear French, with cover names in clear beside them (E: E:, F: F:, A, C, D, L). Samples read at viewer zoom, single glyphs uncertain. Scan 2, last lines: 'provisionnellement 76a5ug0 463h56a2 874ed5aq u7 g0deges 24M5u56a2 4e25e05n7. Il s'y rendra'. Scan 6, lines 1-2: 'Si C n'a pas communiqué jusqu'ici a F: F: 703u567n3672 4609m2570e465m3246009754 21732r0976e4236, qu'il lui a envoié'. Scan 8: 'ce que A a dit a 67035524609732en875 he4056 907713625e4370.' Groups such as 67, 46, 4609 and 975 recur. No decipherment between the lines or in the margin on scans 2, 6, 7 or 8; the marginal text on scans 4, 6 and 8 is clear French from the writer. Earlier scans 1, 4, 20, 30, 55 were correct that they hold no digits, but they missed the four leaves that do.

vetting.key_check: Key inv. 126 tested only in part, and it did not open the strings. Cover names on these leaves do match its tables (scan 1 and scan 2). 'Supplement du Chiffre' (scan 9) gives pairs 42-89 only: paired from the start, the scan 8 string gives 67 N, then 03 and 24, and the scan 6 string 46 C, then 09, all outside the table, and the strings also hold letter forms the table has no place for. The letter table on scan 5 (a x, b r, c p ...) substitutes letters, not digits. Key sheets read: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 19, 20; sheets 6, 7, 8, 14, 16, 18 were seen only as thumbnails, which look like versos. No full transcription or solver run was done, so the digit system of the strings is not established.
vetting.key_in_volume: Gelders Archief 0439 inv. 126, 'Sleutels tot het geheimschrift, 1730, 1731', 20 scans online. Scan 1 'Extract uit het groot Chyffer': Rosendael E:E:, Veldwen D:D:, de Burggraaf C:C:, Torck F:F:, Chesterfield O, and others. Scan 2: more cover names and signs. Scan 3 and 15: numbered lists (30 de Hr v. Ittersum, 70 Deventer, 800 Luisius, 900 Grumbkow ...). Scan 5: letter-for-letter table. Scan 9 'Supplement du Chiffre': A 42/43 to Z 88/89. Scan 11 'No 6': another cover list. Scan 19: printed 'Table de Chiffre' with instructions.

entries.title: Diego Hurtado de Mendoza (imperial ambassador in Rome) → Ferrante Gonzaga, letter with enclosures partly in cipher
entries.correspondents: Diego Hurtado de Mendoza → Ferrante Gonzaga
entries.shelfmark: Biblioteca Estense Universitaria, Modena, Autografoteca Campori, Lettera H, Hurtado de Mendoza, Diego, sfasc. I, cc. 40-46
entries.folio_note: 14 canvases; enclosures cc. 42-44 with lines of symbol cipher and a list of names (possibly a partial key or a clear summary).
entries.status: Record: 'Le cc. 42-44 contengono allegati alla lettera, alcuni cifrati.' Hurtado de Mendoza appears in Dan's repo for other archives, not for this item. The other ~95 Hurtado de Mendoza records here were checked: none mentions cipher. Manifest uuid(s): e02077fa-33a9-4749-b581-f88f2d45e9be. Compare with the Hurtado de Mendoza key of open PR #216 (mendoza1548), same sender a year earlier; not tested. Brice Dudout's note (issue #254, PR #265, 5 Nov 2026), not yet reconciled with the vetting above: he reads c. 44r as the ciphered enclosure (17 lines, about 400 signs) and c. 42r as its contemporary decipherment, a shorter sheet laid over 44 beginning 'Y quando huvieremos dado la auctoridad a los ocho...', with a sign-by-sign alignment of 340 of 376 signs; the vetting read cc. 40r-42r as the letter in clear. The two readings of c. 42r conflict: look at c. 42r before relying on either. Both agree the place is Siena ('en Sena iij de abril 1549'), not Rome. Prior print: none found; not checked: Vazquez & Selden Rose, Algunas cartas... 1538-1552 (Yale 1945), and Varo Zafra, Cartas (Granada 2016). Lead found by WAINUT.
entries.why: Charles V's ambassador in Rome writing to the governor of Milan during the Parma-Piacenza crisis of 1549. Follow-up (issue #254): useful for mendoza1548, the same chancery syllabary with a neighbouring key. 10 of the 11 sure 1548 values that recur in 1549 keep their value (n=a, mo=s, ω=e, que, y...), while the 1549 inventory has signs absent from the 1548 pairs, so the 44r/42r pair extends that key.
entries.verify: Read the list on c. 43 at full size: if it pairs names with signs, it is a key.

seen.extent: 14 canvases. cc.40r-42r letter in clear Spanish, 'Illmo y Exmo Sr', about 100 lines over four pages, signed by Mendoza, closing 'en Sena ... de abril 1549'; c.43r-43v a loose slip with a clear list of heads of business (about 18 lines), photographed lying over the cipher sheet; c.44r one page of about 20 lines wholly in cipher (c.44v shows only the bleed-through of it); c.45v address 'Al Illmo y Exmo Sr Don Fernando Gonzaga' with the note 'Don Diego de Mendoza, de abril'; cc.46r-46v a second leaf in clear Spanish with 3 cipher lines in the sentence on c.46v.
seen.cipher: Syllabic or nomenclator signs with word spaces and points (curved and barred letter-like signs, e.g. a ꝓ-like and ∂-like family) filling c.44r from top to bottom, and three lines on c.46v after 'Al capitan Tapia en Massa, la qual ...'. The slip on c.43r is clear Spanish, not cipher: a list of heads ('del sacar de la gente', 'de los 4000 ducados del donativo', 'de los de Rauena', 'Mendoca en Orbitello y Porto Ercole', 'Tapia en Massa') that reads as an agenda or summary and gives no signs. On c.46v a clear marginal note of about six lines ('por fas o nefas se tenga ... el tiempo se resolvera ... el Trivulcio ... el Rey y a los hijos') stands beside the 3 cipher lines; I could not tell whether it paraphrases them or is part of the letter, and it is not an interlinear decipherment. No decipherment is written between the lines of c.44r, which is the main cipher, and no clear copy of it is bound with it. Note: the closing says Siena, not Rome (Mendoza was governor of Siena).

entries.title: 'Francesco Rota' → 'Mons. Vatron' in London, The Hague 8 Apr 1624, mostly in code
entries.correspondents: 'Francesco Rota' (per Goetz and Gardiner the Capuchin P. Alexander of Hales) → 'Mons. Vatron', London
entries.shelfmark: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10398 (Collectio Camerariana vol. 48), n. 106
entries.folio_note: Clm 10398 scan 469 (fol. 233).
entries.status: Ciphertext only; not the camerarius1621 system (issue #254). One page (bsb00116447 view 469, fol. 233r; 233v is blank). Italian clear with 104 two-digit groups (10-94, written together by words) and isolated letter-signs; no gloss or contemporary decipherment. It is not the Camerarius 1621-22 system (camerarius1621): that system is a nomenclator with groups of 40-3200, here there is no group of 100 or more, and only 3 of the 104 groups have a value in that key. A fresh attack also failed: its score did not beat the shuffled-key control. Prior-print risk: Rusdorf's Mémoires (1789) and Consilia et negotia (1725); Rusdorf was the Palatine envoy in London in 1622-27 and is probably 'Vatron' (not verified). Lead found by WAINUT. Earlier note: Halm, Verzeichniss der handschriftlichen Sammlung der Camerarii (1874), p. 95: "Lettera di Francesco Rota à Mr. Vatron à Londre, Haia 8 Apr. 1624 (von Lud. Cam. geschrieben, grossentheils in Chiffern)". Cover names: n. 107 is 'Francesco Rota al Sign. Lod. Camerario, Bruxelles 29 Apr.', so 'Rota' is a cover used in this channel. Mostly cipher; Italian plaintext. Not on DECODE (repo dumps have no BSB Clm 103xx). Image: https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/en/view/bsb00116447?page=1 (IIIF https://api.digitale-sammlungen.de/iiif/presentation/v2/bsb00116447/manifest). Viewed by WAINUT on 3 Nov 2026 (scan 469): Italian clear text with run-together two-digit numbers and the letters g, p, t, c, x and & as code signs; no decipherment on the page, so ciphertext-only. Names the Capuchin Giacinto ('Non erubesco Evangelium', cf. n. 108). Not the code of Camerarius's 1621-22 letters to Solms (WAINUT's separate camerarius1621 submission). Not attempted.
entries.why: A cover-named letter from the Capuchin mission of 1623-24, in two-digit code with letter signs. Halm says Ludwig Camerarius wrote it, which would make this leaf a copy; the hand was not checked. Follow-up (issue #254): check Rusdorf's Mémoires (1789) and Consilia et negotia (1725) for this letter before any further attack.

prior_art.lasry: Web search on Lasry with Camerarius and Palatine cipher 1624 returned only unrelated papers (Mary Stuart, Catholic League); known.py finds no Rota or Vatron row among the repo's Lasry material.
prior_art.edition: Rusdorf, Mémoires et négociations secrètes (ed. Cuhn, 1789), Google Books full view kmZeAAAAcAAJ (hits run to p. 702; volume number not checked), searched inside: it covers the Rota mission from London at length (Feb 1624, pp. 161-275; Rota resolved to go to The Hague, p. 252; dispatched, p. 253) and prints letters of April 1624 (pp. 280-300), but 'Vatron' and 'Watron' give 0 hits, 'Haye 8 Avril' 0, 'Rota Camerarius' 0, and 'chiffre' only pp. 163 and 265, neither this letter. The volume labelled Volume 2 (M4B-0ou3Tb0C) gave 0 on every term, including '1624', so its search did not work and it was not read; kmZeAAAAcAAJ already runs well past April 1624 (hits to Dec 1624 and beyond), so the date falls there. Khevenhüller, Annales Ferdinandei Tom. X (1623-27), MDZ bsb10866796, full-text API: 'Vatron', 'Watron', 'Rusdorf', 'Camerarius' 0; 'Rota' once, an unrelated auditor (scan 686); the Capuchin mission is at pp. 422-423 (scan 231, read), Maximilian denying he ever gave the Capuchin a commission and naming Pater Jacinto and the nuncio at Brussels as the ones who could show it, with no letter of 8 April and no cipher. Goetz, Briefe und Akten N.F. II/1 (1907), opened in full text by the first pass (archive.org briefeundaktenz00duchgoog): prints Coll. Camerariana XLVIII n. 108, summarises n. 107 and n. 110, quotes n. 111, has no Vatron and does not cite n. 106. Söltl, Religionskrieg, full text: Rota at The Hague March-April 1624, no Vatron.
prior_art.literature: Gardiner, History of England V ch. XLVII and Krüner, Johann von Rusdorf (1876) describe the mission without this letter. Schubert, Ludwig Camerarius (1955/2013) is not online and was not seen. Searches on Rota, Vatron and cipher found no decipherment.

vetting.key_check: camerarius1621 key.tsv does not fit: its code is German and one-part, with groups up to about 3200, while this letter uses two-digit numbers and letter signs in Italian. Not attempted. Goetz cites Hyacinth and Alexander reports in cipher ('Chiffr. Or./Abschr.', Munich St.A. K. schw. 442/19), an untested possible route to the same family; no key found on record.

entries.title: Letter to an ecclesiastical elector (?), Osnabrück 13 Aug 1633, written in cipher

Microfilm (black and white) scan of Clm 10415 (Collectio Camerariana vol. 65), fol. 161, old piece number '58' in the margin.
seen.extent: One page: a ruled frame of about 28 lines of cipher (counted by eye from the 1400 px image, not by machine), about 4-5 groups per line; scan 330 (verso) is blank.
seen.cipher: Framed block of word-divided groups of digits mixed with letter and sign characters (e.g. '2047oEi', '203y205bo', '250100', 'Sarbo', 'bo4304'), one line struck through; above it the clear salutation 'Rme Illme Princeps ac Domine Dne Clementissime', below it the clear dateline '... Raptissime Osnabrugi 1633 13 Aug.' (the reading of the first word of the dateline is uncertain), the clear closing 'Rmae et Illmae Celsitudinis Vrae ... Humillimus et obedientissimus Servus' and a signature that looks like 'C. L.' with a flourish. No plaintext, interlinear gloss or marginal decipherment is written on the frame or the page; the page has only faint show-through, which is not a gloss. No key table on the leaf.

prior_art.lasry: Web search 'Osnabrück 1633 Chiffre Camerarius Oxenstierna Knyphausen Wartenberg entziffert' found only a Tartu paper on the decipherment of a German letter from Heusner von Wandersleben to Oxenstierna (1637), a different letter, and nothing on this one; no GL.htm entry.
prior_art.edition: Halm 1874 p. 164 records it as 'in Chiffern geschrieben' with no decipherment. Bierther, Briefe und Akten N.F. II/8 (1982), the only edition volume that could cover this date for Bavarian and League business, was opened again in Google Books on 4 Nov 2026 and shows 'Preview unavailable' (no search inside); the earlier batch c25 searched its snippets for 13 Aug 1633 with Osnabrück and Chiffre and found no entry. A letter in the Palatine Camerariana from besieged Osnabrück is not obviously in a Bavarian-political edition, but that is not excluded. Oxenstierna's Rikskansleren skrifter and Swedish-Palatine editions not opened.
prior_art.literature: Three web searches (Osnabrück 13 Aug 1633 Chiffern Camerariana Clm 10415; Brief in Ziffern Belagerung Knyphausen Wartenberg entziffert; earlier batch's Cryptologia/HistoCrypt searches) found only the 1633 Swedish siege of Osnabrück (14 Aug to 11 Sep 1633), other Camerariana items (Clm 10404 Oxenstierna invitation) and no study or decipherment of this letter.

No key table was seen on this leaf and the neighbouring pieces were not searched for one in this pass.

The lead's own shelfmark and links name Clm 10416 / bsb00116464, but the letter is in Clm 10415 / bsb00116463 scan 329.

seen.extent: Digit runs inside a clear Italian letter: 44r about 7 lines at the foot, 44v about 20 lines mixed with short clear stretches, 46r 4 lines mid-page, 46v 3 lines at the foot above the dateline 'Da Bolduch alli xi di decemb. 1545' and the signature 'Camillo Capilupo'; roughly 1,200 digits by eye, not counted by machine. 45r-45v are clear Italian prose. After the 46r run the clear text goes on with news (Queen Maria at Utrecht, English ambassadors, the Turk before Buda), so the digits are inserts in the letter.
seen.cipher: Continuous strings of digits with no word division, vertical strokes marking some breaks, a few clear words intercalated on 44v (e.g. 'allhora fu forza che', 'della qual cosa resagli la causa', 'onde con questo adito', 'Appresso gli ricordai la importanza ch'era alle cose di parma et di piacenza'); one underlined run on 44v. Digit groups run on, so the unit size is not visible. The clear Italian before and after each run is the covering letter and is not a decipherment of the digits: it differs from them in length and sense, and no interlinear or marginal plaintext is written over, under or beside any run on cc. 44r, 44v, 45r, 45v, 46r or 46v. No key table on the leaves.

entries.title: Tierra Firme: five cipher letters, 13 folios (AGI Indiferente 737 no. 171); the first letter is deciphered in Panama 29
entries.correspondents: Alvaro de Sosa, governor of Tierra Firme (first letter) and others → officials at Seville / Consejo de Indias
entries.shelfmark: AGI, Indiferente General, 737, N.171 (PARES 300401); decipherment of letter 1 in AGI, Panama, 29, R.6, N.23
entries.folio_note: "Cinco cartas cifradas. S.F. 13 f." Four of the five have no decipherment named; images online (PARES flags IMG).
entries.status: PARES description (read 4 Nov 2026): "Cinco cartas cifradas ... Nota: El texto descifrado de la primera carta se halla en el legajo Panama,29,R.6,N.23 (Copia de carta de Alvaro de Sosa, Gobernador de Tierra Firme a los oficiales de Sevilla, 1554, Julio, 4. 2 + 2 f.)". entries.title: Mihaly Teleki to Nalaczi, Haller, Apafi, Szepesi, Szalai and Rhedey: 13 letters in number cipher before the 1678 campaign
entries.correspondents: Mihaly Teleki (chancellor of Transylvania) -> Istvan Nalaczi, Janos Haller, Mihaly Apafi, Pal Szepesi, Pal Szalai, Ferenc Rhedey
entries.shelfmark: Teleki Mihaly levelezese VIII (ed. S. Gergely, Budapest 1926) nos. 9, 10, 20, 21, 25, 30, 36, 38, 41, 43, 50, 79, 87 (pp. 9-96); copies from Teleki's chancery letter-book (Lang IDs C.Tel.04, 05, 07, 08, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21, 22)
entries.folio_note: 13 short letters, numbers 1-79 (about 37 distinct values), printed in the edition; Hegedus read C.Tel.15 only (23 Jan 1678)
entries.status: Lang lists all 13 as "megfejtetlen" (numbers, probably homophonic) and the editor did not solve them. Hegedus (NyelvVilag 23, 2020) worked through C.Tel.15 (to Rhedey, 23 Jan 1678) as a monoalphabetic number code and says the key from Teleki's 1666 letter does not fit it: a different clavis was used. The others of Jan-Mar 1678 probably share that clavis. The letter-book is probably DECODE R4819-R4834 (Cluj Reformed diocese; records with no images or decryption; not matched record by record).
entries.why: Transylvania's war council writing in cipher on the eve of the Thokoly/kuruc campaign into Upper Hungary (June 1678).
entries.verify: Obtain Teleki Mihaly levelezese VIII (Arcanum, MEK or a library copy); take the C.Tel.15 key from Hegedus (kripto.blog.hu 2016 and NyelvVilag 23) and run it over C.Tel.04-22; where it fails, solve as monoalphabetic with homophones.

Egy 17. szazadi kodolt uzenet feltorese', NyelvVilag 23 (2020), pp. 60ff, PDF read 4 Nov 2026: https://publikaciotar.uni-bge.hu/1711/1/Hegedus_Nyelvvilag23.pdf ; it prints the number text of C.Tel.15 from Gergely Samuel (ed.), Teleki Mihaly levelezese VIII (MTT, Budapest 1926) p. 40, no. 38. The repertory of the 13 letters: Lang Benedek, Titkositas a kora ujkori Magyarorszagon (MTA thesis 2015), pp. 286-287, https://real-d.mtak.hu/922/7/dc_758_13_doktori_mu.pdf , read 4 Nov 2026. Gergely vol. VIII is not on Hungaricana (reviews only) or free elsewhere that I found; the lead has no access value.
seen.extent: Seen: one letter, C.Tel.15, 23 Jan 1678, about 240 numbers of 37 distinct values (1-79), clear first and last sentences. Not seen: the other letters of the lead (Gergely VIII nos. 9, 10, 20, 21, 25, 30, 36, 38, 41, 43, 50, 79, 87; short number-cipher letters, Lang IDs C.Tel.04, 05, 07, 08, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 19, 21 etc.).
seen.cipher: Lang's repertory marks C.Tel.04, 05, 07, 08, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19 and 21 'magyar, szamok, valoszinuleg homof.' and 'megfejtetlen'; 10 and 18 'reszben feloldva, reszben megfejtetlen'. Hegedus (2020): 'A titkosírások megoldásával a kötetek kiadói sem boldogultak, vagy talán nem is próbálkoztak' (the volume editors did not solve the number sequences). The printed C.Tel.15 is number strings with the first and last sentences in clear and a short bracketed remark, no decipherment printed; his own solution is the article. Gap in what I saw: only C.Tel.15 was read as text; for the others I rely on Lang and Hegedus.

prior_art.decode: The letter-book copies are probably DECODE R4819-R4834 (Cluj, Eparhia Reformata, Pokoly-Nagy G2 506, 1650-1690; local list shows all 16 as status 4, Hungarian cleartext, no decipherment listed); not matched record by record and no images on the list. Teleki's own cipher keys are DECODE R647-R651, R665-R673 (NAH P1238 Teleki Mihaly Collection, cipher keys, 1660-1690, plus R648 for Ferenc Nadasdy 1671). No decipherment of the 1678 letters in the local list.

prior_art.edition: Gergely Samuel, Teleki Mihaly levelezese VIII (1678-1679), Budapest 1926, prints the ciphers as number strings and does not decipher the ones Lang lists (Lang 2015 pp. 286-287; Hegedus 2020). prior_art.literature: Hegedus 2020 is the only decipherment found (C.Tel.15, plus his 2016 blog post on a different letter, Teleki to Szechy Maria, 1666: https://kripto.blog.hu/2016/03/12/mit_irt_teleki_mihaly_szechy_marianak_1666_juliusaban ). Lang, Real Life Cryptology (AUP 2018) describes Hungarian ciphers in general; no other reading of the 1678 letters found.

Lang's T.Tel.02 (clavis dated 30 July 1677, MOL P 1238, printed by Szilagyi) and the undated P 1238 keys on DECODE (R647-R673) were not tried either.

entries.correspondents: Carl Fredrik von Höpken and Edvard Carlson -> the chancery president (Gyllenborg) and the King

entries.folio_note: 567 images (R0003637). Image 227: a French "extrait de la traduction" of a letter with whole lines of four-digit numbers and French written between them; image 482: a Swedish letter of 22 Sept 1742 with three number blocks glossed in Swedish; underlined interlinear passages also at about 29, 86, 114, 397, 539 (thumbnails).
entries.status: Catalogue: plain letters to the chancery president. Same four-digit code as the sibling volumes 9/20-9/23 and 9/29; glosses written over the numbers show the passages were read on receipt.
entries.why: The last Höpken-Carlson volume (1742, after the Swedish defeat in Finland): the Ottoman side of the Hat government's foreign policy, with plaintext cribs for every passage.
entries.verify: View images 227 and 482 at full size; transcribe, align numerals and glosses, and pool with 9/20-9/23 to rebuild the whole code.

In the 47-image sample about 10 spreads carry bare four-digit runs set in clear Swedish (198, 246, 342, 378, 438, 450, 474, 486, 510, 522; image 342 alone has about 50 lines of numbers) and about 20 carry glossed passages (e.g. 29, 86, 114, 227, 397, 539); the rest are clear text or blank versos. Not paged leaf by leaf, so counts are by sampling.
seen.cipher: Four-digit numeric code, values about 1000-2900, in Swedish and French despatches of Hopken and Carlson, Jan-Dec 1742 (dockets 19 Feb, 8/19 Apr, 10/21 May, 27 Oct). Image 198 (8/19 April 1742) and 246 (10/21 May 1742): number runs inside clear Swedish with no gloss, no interlinear text, no key on the leaf. Image 342: two full pages of numbers, no gloss. In the glossed passages (image 227 French 'Extrait de la traduction de la lettre du Chan de Crimee', 29 Latin, 86 and 114 Swedish, 397, 539 French) a plaintext word is written over each number run, so those are cribs, not part of the open text.

entries.title: Duportail → Gouverneur Morris: cypher message sent through Thomas Pinckney, with Morris's transcription, and two Pinckney notes enclosing messages in cypher
entries.correspondents: General Duportail → Gouverneur Morris, via Thomas Pinckney (London); Thomas Pinckney → Morris
entries.shelfmark: Columbia RBML, Gouverneur Morris papers, 1768-1816, Box 3, items 241, 1094 and 1099
entries.folio_note: 241: transcription in Morris's hand of a cypher message and the message in cypher, 4 p.; 1094: unsigned note, [May 1794?], 1 p. enclosing a message in cypher; 1099: Pinckney, London, 23 Aug 1794, 1 p. enclosing a message in cypher
entries.status: Columbia finding aid (read 4 Nov 2026): item 241 "transcription, in Morris' hand, of cypher message transmitted to Morris through Thomas Pinckney ... and message in cypher, 4 p."; 1094 and 1099 each "enclosing message in cypher". The wording does not say whether Morris's "transcription" is of the cipher groups or of a decipherment. No edition or study of these found.
entries.why: Morris was being recalled from Paris in the summer of 1794 and his diary has a gap from January to October 1794; a message from a French officer-engineer sent through Pinckney in London is exactly what that gap lacks. Morris and Pinckney had swapped and lost cyphers in 1793 (Pinckney to Jefferson), so the system may be a Morris-Pinckney cypher.

entries.verify: Order items 241, 1094, 1099 from Columbia RBML (reproductions allowed for research); compare the Founders Online Pinckney letters of 1793 for the cypher.
